entry.title: httpi: the internet protocol to reduce compute from misbehaving agents

author.name: joao_abrantes

entry.summary: This proposal argues AI safety should shift from purely training-based approaches toward mechanism design, drawing an analogy to how societies keep humans safe by assigning accountability and imposing costs (fines, lost access, deposits) on misbehavior. The author sketches httpi, an internet protocol concept where misbehaving AI agents lose resources or access, treating post-deployment incentive structures rather than in-model training as the primary safety lever.

entry.title: Voice or Stereotype? Disentangling Acoustic and Content-Based Gender in Speech-to-Speech Models

author.name: Xiaoqun Liu, Tanu Mitra, Harshit Rajgarhia, Abhishek Mukherji

entry.summary: The paper studies whether speech-to-speech models treat a speaker according to their voice or according to content-based gender stereotypes, addressing the methodological problem that fixed hard-coded output voices mask bias. It distinguishes voice-rendering bias from stated-gender judgments and tests whether models follow acoustic cues or content stereotypes. This is a novel fairness evaluation angle specific to speech models.

entry.title: Improving Cross-Lingual Token Representations by Adding a Pinch of SALT

author.name: Guillem Ram\'irez

entry.summary: SALT is a lightweight post-training method injecting span-level supervision into cross-lingual sentence encoders to improve token representations for tasks like sequence tagging and hallucination detection. It achieves best results on four of five multilingual token-level benchmarks while preserving sentence-level quality. The work addresses the train-usage mismatch in multilingual sentence encoders.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Sea-Ice Type Mapping with Multiple Ice Charts

author.name: Samira Alkaee Taleghan, Younghyun Koo, Andrew P. Barrett, Farnoush Banaei-Kashani

entry.summary: The paper addresses deep-learning-based mapping of sea-ice stage of development using operational ice charts, explicitly modeling the fact that analyst-produced labels are uncertain and represent ranges of compatible thicknesses. It fuses multiple ice charts with uncertainty awareness rather than treating chart annotations as exact ground truth. This improves the trustworthiness of automated sea-ice products used for navigation and operational monitoring.

entry.title: Unthrottling the Tanh Jacobian in SAC: A Negative Result on Bang-Bang Control and MetaDrive

author.name: Faiq Shamass

entry.summary: The paper tests whether the vanishing tanh Jacobian in Soft Actor-Critic starves the actor of critic signal when extreme actions are optimal, proposing a minimal auxiliary loss term that restores detached action-gradient signal. Across a bang-bang double integrator and MetaDrive experiments, the intervention yields no meaningful benefit, since vanilla SAC already achieves near-optimal return.

entry.title: Odometer-Agnostic Drift Correction Using OpenStreetMap Lane Geometry

author.name: Joaquin Caballero, Emilio Garcia-Fidalgo, Alberto Ortiz, Jarno Ralli

entry.summary: A lightweight, open-source method that corrects long-term odometry drift by aligning short trajectory segments to sparse OpenStreetMap lane centerlines, working online without dense maps or expensive preprocessing across LiDAR and visual odometry backends. A pragmatic map-assisted localization contribution leveraging freely available map data. Useful for large-scale or loop-free environments.

entry.title: When will average people feel AI’s impact?

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert argues that comparisons of the AI boom to the industrial revolution miss that most people lack tangible new goods from AI and that society has more inertia than in prior technological transitions. Drawing on his time offline, he observes that current consumer touch-points for AI are fringe, marginally beneficial, or confusing, and explores when diffusion into everyday life might actually occur.

entry.title: CT-SAFR: Safe and Interpretable Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Autonomous Robots: A Multi-Layered Verification Framework for Trustworthy AI-Driven Robotic Decision Making

author.name: Cagri Temel

entry.summary: Presents CT-SAFR, a multi-layered verification framework for chain-of-thought reasoning in autonomous robots, reporting 94.2% hallucination detection with sub-500ms latency and an 87% reduction in unsafe reasoning outputs in a warehouse robot case study. Motivated by evidence that reasoning models verbalize their true decision process only 25-39% of the time. Targets safe deployment of reasoning LLMs in physical robotics.

entry.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation

author.name: Sudaksh Kalra, Dolly Sapra

entry.summary: Elastoformer transforms conventional neural networks into Elastic NNs that can dynamically scale computation at runtime to match fluctuating latency, power, and memory constraints on edge devices. This targets the mismatch between fixed execution flows of standard DNNs and the dynamic operating conditions of EdgeAI vision systems. The framework supports real-time elastic adaptation without retraining per configuration.

entry.title: Future-Aware Flow Planning for Safe UAV Target Following

author.name: Boning Feng, Haoran Zhang, Xiaowen Bi, Yanzhen Zhang, Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: A flow-based planner for UAV target following that uses predicted target futures as residual signals for trajectory generation and embeds risk-scored executable-prefix repair inside the sampling loop. Improves the safety-tracking trade-off with zero in-distribution collision rate and the lowest out-of-distribution collision rate on receding-horizon benchmarks. Honest framing about trade-offs rather than dominating all metrics.

entry.title: Valerant: An Automatic Navigable Game Map Generator via Action-Conditioned World Model Exploration

author.name: Yiran Qiao, Feng Wang, Jing Ma

entry.summary: Extends World Action Models to 3D games with Valerant, a system that automatically generates navigable game maps by coupling action-conditioned world modeling with exploration, addressing the lack of persistent 3D geometry in prior 2D game-oriented approaches.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Imitation: Contrastive Modeling for Reasoning Path Alignment in Multimodal In-Context Learning

author.name: Mingbo Yang, Wenqiang Wang, Zhaolu Kang, Peng Chen, Yannan Chen, Sunshang Wang, Yan Xiao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal ICL framework combining contrastive demonstration modeling with self-refinement so that model responses align with the reasoning path required by the input rather than imitating surface features of demonstrations. This targets a recognized limitation of multimodal in-context learning on complex tasks. The direction is sensible but the approach is a fairly standard combination of known techniques.

entry.title: From Plausible to Actionable: A Position on LLM Self-Explanations

author.name: Elize Herrewijnen, Benedetta Muscato, Gizem Gezici, Fosca Giannotti

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that LLM self-explanations can be highly plausible and questionably faithful yet still actionable, and that standard XAI evaluation protocols fit LLM-generated explanations poorly. The authors propose practical evaluation directions tailored to self-explanations. It contributes a conceptual reframing for the explainable AI community.

entry.title: From Fixed Keys to Readable Schemas: Small Language Models for Vehicle Agent Function Calls

author.name: Hamed Jafarzadeh Asl, Yuanhao Yu, Vahid Partovi Nia

entry.summary: Studies how small language models for in-vehicle assistants should represent callable functions: dedicated functional tokens versus schema-in-prompt prompting. The authors release a benchmark of 9,822 single-turn examples across 79 vehicle functions, showing the compactness-generalization tradeoff between the two approaches. Relevant to on-device agentic function calling under tight latency and memory budgets.

entry.title: NOPE-HYPE: A Structured Simulation Workflow for Robust Speech-to-Text Across Diverse Acoustic Environments

author.name: Niramay M. Patel, Bibek Behera, Raksha Sharma

entry.summary: NOPE-HYPE combines a controllable acoustic environment simulator, coverage-optimal environment reduction on PSD templates, and interpretable hyperparameter search to systematically train and evaluate robust speech-to-text. Simulator-generated noise matches balanced real-noise training for Whisper and SeamlessM4T models. The workflow addresses the scarcity of diverse acoustic conditions in speech training data.

entry.title: Hierarchical and Permutation-Invariant Feature Transformation Learning via Policy-Guided Embedding Search

author.name: Rui Liu, Tao Zhe, Yanyong Huang, Sankha Narayan Guria, Xiao Luo, Wei Fan, Yanjie Fu, Dongjie Wang

entry.summary: This paper addresses automated feature transformation for tabular data, identifying three limitations of recent generative embedding-space approaches: ignored hierarchy between features, operations, and abstractions; order-sensitive embeddings imposed on permutation-invariant transformation sequences; and ill-suited gradient-based search in non-convex spaces. The authors propose a framework combining a permutation-invariant hierarchical representation with policy-guided (reinforcement learning based) search over transformation strategies. This matters for automated ML since feature transformation strongly affects predictive performance on tabular data.

entry.title: Applying foundation model embeddings towards urban livability evaluation

author.name: Ayush Khot, Wen Zhou, Shaowen Wang

entry.summary: This paper investigates which physical features are encoded in geospatial foundation model embeddings such as AlphaEarth, AnySat, and TerraMind, and provides a systematic framework for identifying the most predictive geospatial indicators for urban livability. The work targets socioeconomic measurement in data-scarce regions where high-resolution satellite data is abundant. It offers practical guidance on which embedding sources and features matter for policy-relevant prediction.

entry.title: A practical DIRECT-type algorithm for medium-scale black-box global optimization

author.name: Linas Stripinis, Remigijus Paulavi\v{c}ius

entry.summary: The paper introduces X-DTC-GL, a DIRECT-type deterministic global optimization algorithm that extends the classic method from low-dimensional to medium-scale problems. It uses dynamic partitioning driven by local one-dimensional surrogate models to rapidly subdivide promising hyper-rectangles, plus hybridization with hill-climbing. This matters for black-box optimization tasks such as hyperparameter tuning and engineering design where gradients are unavailable and dimensionality defeats existing DIRECT methods.

entry.title: Bridging Theory and Data: Correcting Nuclear Mass Models with Interpretable Machine Learning

author.name: Yanhua Lu, Tianshuai Shang, Pengxiang Du, Jian Li, Haozhao Liang

entry.summary: The study applies Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) to refine nuclear mass predictions, halving the RMSE from 0.3 MeV to 0.16 MeV in a KAN-WS4 hybrid model. Exploiting KAN interpretability, feature importance analysis identifies proton number as the dominant residual driver, suggesting systematic biases in proton-related terms of existing theoretical models. This exemplifies interpretable scientific machine learning where the model both improves predictions and yields physics insights.

entry.title: Bayesian deep learning integration of geophysical and drilling data for 3D prediction of copper mineralization and drill targeting: a case study from the Kogodai prospect, Rudny Altai

author.name: Margarita Veshchezerova, Egor Barashov, Evgenii Gusev, Michael R. Perelshtein, Arlan Kasymzhan, Bolat M. Kabaziev, Nurlan Y. Askarov

entry.summary: The authors present an uncertainty-aware 3D workflow that fuses desurveyed drilling data, trench assays, and geophysical inversions using Bayesian deep learning to predict copper mineralization fields and prioritize drill targets at the Kogodai prospect in the Rudny Altai. The approach aims to extract hidden value from existing brownfield data and shorten time-to-discovery in structurally complex terranes. It demonstrates a credible pipeline for uncertainty-quantified mineral exploration.

entry.title: X-amine509: Predicting the Practical Risk Level of Enterprise X.509 Certificates

author.name: Cameron Keith, Shubh Patel, JD Kilgallin, Caleb Shorter

entry.summary: X-amine509 is a two-stage triage system that uses machine learning to rank enterprise X.509 certificates by predicted risk, routing only the highest-risk items to expensive deterministic analysis. Risk is a composite score from 177 defect checks grounded in CA/Browser Forum Baseline Requirements, NIST guidance, and cryptographic strength criteria across four severity tiers. It addresses a real operational scaling problem in managing millions of certificates.

entry.title: Efficient Graph Neural Networks for Multicarrier Wideband Hybrid Beamforming Optimization

author.name: Beier Li, Mai Vu

entry.summary: Uses GNNs over a bipartite graph representation, where a shared analog beamformer connects to multiple subcarriers, to optimize hybrid beamforming in wideband 6G systems affected by beam squinting. The paper develops three GNN architectures with different digital beamformer representations as a cost-effective signal-processing alternative to per-antenna true-time-delay hardware.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Multi-Task Surrogate Model for the Martian Nightside Thermosphere

author.name: Sergey Nikiforov

entry.summary: A multi-task physics-informed neural network predicts logarithmic densities of four neutral species (O, CO2, N2, Ar) in the Martian nightside thermosphere using over a decade of MAVEN/NGIMS observations. A shared backbone with species-specific heads plus a weak monotonicity prior enforced via automatic differentiation prevents non-physical artifacts like density inversions in sparsely sampled regimes.

entry.title: X2-NativeCursor: Native-Token Text Progress Tracking for Incremental-Text Streaming Codec TTS

author.name: Zehan Liu, Carl Chen, Rime Wen, Kaiqi Fu, Altman Lin, Shawn Qin, Lights Shi, Roy Gan, Hao Wang, Qian Wang

entry.summary: X2-NativeCursor is a lightweight observer that tracks speech progress directly from native codec tokens in incremental-text streaming TTS, before waveform decoding, enabling synchronized highlighting, interruption handling, and dialogue-history updates. It links spoken labels to original text spans via a normalization plan and a local matcher over text and native-token encoders. This solves a practical latency problem in real-time conversational speech systems.

entry.title: 5-Dialects-BN: Unmasking the Impact of Transliteration on Bangla Dialectal LLMs

author.name: Md Mahir Jawad, Galib Mahmud Jim, Rafid Ahmed, Mir Sazzat Hossain, Md Fahim, Md Farhad Alam Bhuiyan

entry.summary: The paper presents 5-Dialects-BN, the first multi-annotation benchmark for Bangla dialects, with 6,000 manually annotated entries across five regional varieties aligning Romanized transliteration, dialectal text, Standard Bangla, English, and subjectivity labels. It enables development and evaluation of dialect-aware LLM systems for Bangla, the world's sixth most spoken language, which is underserved by existing Standard-Bangla-only resources.

entry.title: Integrating Unimodal and Vision-Language Representations in Latent Space for Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification

author.name: Quang-Huy Tran, Duc-Tuan Ngo, Minh-Khoi Nguyen-Bui, Dang-Khoa Bui, Thanh-Trong Tran, Tuan-Khoi Nguyen, Hoang-Anh Ngo

entry.summary: This work fuses unimodal RAD-DINO embeddings with vision-language BioViL-T representations in latent space for 14-label multi-label chest X-ray classification on MIMIC-CXR-JPG. Each branch is refined separately before normalized fusion, and the study clarifies how the embedding sources complement each other. It is an applied medical imaging contribution combining established foundation-model embeddings.

entry.title: VFNet: Multi-View Spatio-Temporal Model for Void Fraction Estimation in Gas-Liquid Two-Phase Flow

author.name: Md Adnan Faisal Hossain, Raghav Rajeev, Kumar Nishant, Justin A Weibel, Satish Kumar, Fengqing Zhu

entry.summary: VFNet is a dual-branch spatio-temporal network that predicts void fraction in gas-liquid two-phase flow from synchronized multi-view videos, combining local dual-view feature fusion with a global spatio-temporal branch, trained partly on simulation data. It avoids intrusive sensors and flow-model assumptions that limit prior methods.

entry.title: ScopeMamba-YOLO: Widening the Perceptual Scope Inward and Outward for Small Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Junjie Fan, Yijun Mai, Linduo Wei, Jiayu Rao, Junmin Bao, Qiushi Jin, Guijia Li, Yong Qi

entry.summary: Proposes a YOLO-style detector for small objects in UAV and remote sensing imagery built on an off-path, zero-gated Mamba selective-scanning principle that decouples long-range context modeling from the convolutional stream. Includes a cascaded global-context module, selective-scan PAN neck, and adaptive multi-scale strip blocks.

entry.title: A Bio-Plausible Visual Neural Network for Locust-Inspired Collision Perception

author.name: Qinbing Fu, Jiani Li, Jiajun Huang, Jigen Peng

entry.summary: This paper presents a biologically plausible neural network inspired by locust LGMD neurons for looming detection and collision avoidance, improving on prior computational models with a spatially isotropic sampling strategy mimicking locust ommatidial organization. The goal is greater robustness in complex, dynamic visual environments. Such neuromorphic collision-perception models are relevant for low-power robotics and drones.

entry.title: AXON: A ROS 2 RMW with Shared-Memory/QUIC Transport and QKD/ML-KEM Key Establishment

author.name: Sergio S\'anchez de la Fuente, Miguel \'Angel Gonz\'alez-Santamarta, Francisco Javier Rodr\'iguez-Lera, Vicente Matell\'an Olivera, \'Angel Manuel Guerrero-Higueras

entry.summary: Presents AXON, an alternative ROS 2 middleware implementation in Rust and C++ using POSIX shared memory for same-host traffic and QUIC remotely, with fail-closed TLS 1.3 configurations supporting hybrid post-quantum key exchange (X25519MLKEM768) and QKD-derived keys via ETSI GS. Addresses transport security and performance gaps in DDS-based ROS 2 middleware. Notable for bringing post-quantum and QKD cryptography into robotics middleware.

entry.title: Recovery Theory for Projected Power Iterations in Permutation Synchronization

author.name: Vahan Huroyan, Gilad Lerman

entry.summary: This statistics/ML paper provides theoretical recovery guarantees for the projected power method in permutation synchronization under sparse uniform corruption, proving exact one-step recovery conditions and block-error contraction results. The analysis covers regimes where observed pairs are sparse and corrupted with uniform permutations. This formalizes when a widely used algorithm provably works.

entry.title: Seven Sources of Physical AI Capability Formation

author.name: Gang Chen

entry.summary: Defines a capability-formation taxonomy for Physical AI, identifying seven non-exclusive sources such as recorded experience, predictive modeling, evaluative interaction, and evolution-driven formation, derived via reconstructive induction over primary studies.

entry.title: Critical initialization destabilizes higher input derivatives in wide scalar-input networks

author.name: Prashant Singh, Pranav Singh

entry.summary: The paper derives mean-field recursions through third order for input-derivative variances in wide randomly initialized networks, showing that at the edge-of-chaos criticality the first-derivative variance stays depth-invariant while second-derivative variance grows linearly when the activation has nonzero curvature. This has direct implications for physics-informed losses, score matching, and derivative regularization. It extends classical signal-propagation theory to higher-order jets.

entry.title: Improving 5G AI-RAN MCS Selection by Predicting Retransmissions

author.name: Tamerlan Aghayev, Maxime Elkael, Michele Polese, Reshma Prasad, Salvatore D'Oro, Yunseong Lee, Koichiro Furueda, Tommaso Melodia

entry.summary: The paper introduces NOSTRAdAMUS, a predictive link-adaptation framework for 5G radio access that adds foresight to existing reactive MCS selection algorithms by predicting retransmissions rather than replacing deployed controllers. It addresses noisy, quickly obsolete channel measurements and HARQ feedback in real-time schedulers. The work is a credible applied ML contribution to AI-native RAN research.

entry.title: A Statistical Approach to Estimating Sample Size of Machine Learning Models

author.name: Dat Phan-Trong, Sunil Gupta, Svetha Venkatesh

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for sample-size determination for nonlinear ML prediction models by approximating them with localized linear representations and evaluating statistical power across local regions. This sidesteps the need to specify predictor-outcome structure a priori as in classical power analysis. Useful for study design where ML models replace conventional regression.

entry.title: The Vibe Shift in Software Engineering: Evaluating AI-Led Conversational Programming for Performance, Cognition, and Responsible Adoption

author.name: Sales G. Aribe Jr., Louie Jay S. Labastida

entry.summary: A mixed-methods study of vibe coding with 30 professional developers and students completing tasks under traditional, AI-assisted, and AI-led conversational conditions, measuring efficiency, cognitive effects, and responsible-adoption considerations. Reports significant differences across conditions using ANOVA and thematic analysis. Timely empirical evidence on an emerging development practice.

entry.title: SA-Profile: Automated Sulcus Angle Profiling from Super-Resolution MRI

author.name: Michael Wehrli, Leo Widmer, Edwin Li, Noel Fiechter, Lorenzo Pettinari, Sidaty El Hadramy, Carol C. Hasler, Philippe C. Cattin

entry.summary: This medical imaging paper presents an automated pipeline for continuous sulcus angle profiling to assess trochlear dysplasia, replacing error-prone single-slice manual MRI measurements. It combines implicit neural representation-based super-resolution of multi-planar MR scans with two U-Net landmark detection models, and evaluates on the public fastMRI dataset. The work matters clinically because sulcus angle measurement is currently sensitive to arbitrary slice selection, and continuous profiling across the trochlear region could improve diagnosis of patellar instability.

entry.title: Development and Validation of a Physics-Guided Machine Learning Extrapolation Framework Using a Classical Transient Diffusion Benchmark

author.name: Ashutosh Yadav, Alok Dubey, Prodyut Ranjan Chakraborty, Harshal Akolekar

entry.summary: This paper builds an extrapolation framework for engineering machine learning models, comparing a Bidirectional LSTM and a Physics-Informed Neural Network on a classical one-dimensional transient diffusion benchmark. The goal is physically consistent predictions outside the training domain, a common failure mode of purely data-driven engineering models. The use of a known analytical benchmark allows rigorous validation of extrapolation behavior that field data cannot easily provide.

entry.title: Real-time and adaptive anomaly detection algorithm for cyclostationary models

author.name: Justyna Witulska, Tomasz Barszcz, Ireneusz Jab{\l}o\'nski, Agnieszka Wy{\l}oma\'nska

entry.summary: PeriodicCALM is a real-time anomaly detection framework for cyclostationary data streams that models cycle-dependent variability so that regular cyclic impulses are ignored while genuine anomalies are isolated. It operates with continuous retraining, addressing false-alarm problems of existing methods that misread phase-dependent variability as anomalies. Applications include condition monitoring of machinery and other periodic signal streams.

entry.title: A Unifying Perspective on Probabilities as Model Predictions

author.name: Benedikt H\"oltgen

entry.summary: Argues that every probability is the output of a prediction method combining an abstraction-construction step and a prediction transformation, unifying Bayesian and frequentist notions and showing that even supposedly objective probabilities are model-dependent. It connects finite calibration criteria to the distribution of utilities from acting on probabilistic predictions.

entry.title: Deterministic Prompting for Speaker-Stable Low-Resource Greek TTS

author.name: Georgios Syllas, Efthymios Georgiou, Kosmas Kritsis, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: Provides a data curation recipe turning Greek audiobook recordings into TTS-ready data via WhisperX alignment, then fine-tunes the 880M multilingual Parler-TTS model. The key finding is that LLM-generated style prompts cause speaker drift at inference, and replacing them with deterministic prompts plus a speaker-specific LoRA on 3.5 hours of data anchors speaker identity while updating only ~5% of parameters.

entry.title: HybridFLow: SDN-Orchestrated Client Partitioning for Hybrid Federated Learning

author.name: Osama Abu Hamdan, Rabin Pandey, Hao Che, Engin Arslan, Md Arifuzzaman

entry.summary: HybridFLow is a closed-loop SDN-driven orchestration framework that partitions clients between synchronous and asynchronous participation in cross-silo federated learning, using the SDN controller's global view of network topology, bottlenecks, and contention. It aims to mitigate stragglers in wide-area deployments.

entry.title: When Does Defendant Statement Matter? A Study of Bias and Persuasion in LLM-Simulated Jurors

author.name: Cho-Ying Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces JuryBench, a benchmark of controversial U.S. criminal cases used to study how defendant courtroom statements influence LLM-simulated jurors, varying defendant background, emotional appeal, and rebuttal strategies. It examines persuasion effects, ideological bias, and background-based affinity in juror agents with diverse ideological profiles. This contributes both a benchmark and a behavioral study relevant to the growing use of LLMs for simulating human decision-making in legal contexts.

entry.title: Who Argues What? Joint Argument-Entity Detection and Classification in Political Debates

author.name: Lucio La Cava, Stefano Francesco Monea, Sergio Greco

entry.summary: The paper introduces DNE-ElecDeb, an entity-enriched version of the USElecDeb debate dataset, and a joint task of detecting and classifying which debate named entities are invoked within arguments. This addresses the gap that argument mining usually annotates spans and roles without a paired entity layer, limiting interpretability of political arguments. It enables richer analysis of political discourse by linking claims and premises to actors, events, and parties.

entry.title: Control Copy-Paste: Controllable Diffusion-Based Augmentation Method for Remote Sensing Few-Shot Object Detection

author.name: Yanxing Liu, Jiancheng Pan, Bingchen Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Control Copy-Paste, a diffusion-based augmentation method for few-shot object detection in optical remote sensing that controls both instance diversity and surrounding context to prevent overfitting to monotonous backgrounds. It extends prior diffusion-augmentation approaches by recognizing that context diversity matters alongside object diversity. The method targets rare-object detection with minimal annotations in remote sensing scenarios.

entry.title: Design and Attitude Control of an Underwater Quadruped Robot

author.name: Davide Molinaroli, Mohit Singh, Kostas Alexis

entry.summary: The paper presents the design, modeling, and experimental validation of a reproducible underwater quadruped robot built with custom waterproof motor housings using off-the-shelf seals. It derives a simplified dynamics model capturing how drag on spherical end effectors transmits torque to a floating base, and validates a closed-loop attitude controller. This extends legged robotics toward amphibious mobility for inspection and environmental monitoring.

entry.title: Agentic AI-enabled Semantic Commissioning of a Cognitive Digital Twin for Reconfigurable Manufacturing

author.name: Yangyang Liu, Xun Xu, Jan Polzer

entry.summary: Presents an agent-based workflow using LangGraph multi-agent orchestration plus RAG to automate construction and debugging of Cognitive Digital Twins in reconfigurable manufacturing, combining document-based semantic extraction with autonomous binding to live industrial telemetry. Bridges modern agentic LLM techniques with industrial digital twin engineering. Relevant as an applied case of agentic AI in manufacturing systems.

entry.title: A Confidence-Aware Multimodal Fusion Framework for Industrial Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Qiqi Dong, Boya Jia, Yi Zhang, Binbin Lian

entry.summary: Proposes CAMF, fusing object 6D pose, gaze, skeletal motion, and IMU hand motion for human intention prediction in industrial HRI, with a confidence-trend-driven dynamic fusion mechanism inside a BiLSTM and confidence-guided balanced learning to suppress noisy modalities. Validated on a UR3 collaborative robot platform. Targets reliability of intent prediction in real factory settings.

entry.title: Frame-Coded Legged Locomotion over Noisy Terrain

author.name: Lav R. Varshney

entry.summary: This theoretical paper reformulates open-loop multilegged locomotion over rough terrain as a quantized finite-frame expansion with erasures, mapping a d-dimensional body command into N heterogeneous contact commands that terrain may erase or corrupt. Unlike prior repetition-coding interpretations, this provides a positive task rate and adaptive decoding as the surviving contact set changes. It imports coding theory concepts into locomotion analysis.

entry.title: Efficient Leakage-Free Neural Architecture Search under Leave-One-Subject-Out Evaluation

author.name: Heinke Hihn

entry.summary: Proposes a leakage-free, block-based NAS approach that shares architecture search runs across subjects, avoiding the O(N^2) cost of fully nested leave-one-subject-out evaluation. On the BioVid Heat Pain dataset it improves mean accuracy from 82.79% to 83.39% while cutting parameters by up to 99.2%. It matters for subject-based biosignal and medical classification where data leakage is a common pitfall.

entry.title: Introducing Consort: A Spec-First Agent Framework for Enforced, Test-Driven Development on Live Database Branches

author.name: Kevin Hartman

entry.summary: Introduces Consort, a spec-first framework for agent-driven software development that enforces test-driven discipline on live database branches, and taxonomizes existing frameworks (Spec Kit, superpowers, BMAD, GSD) by enforcement mode: persuasion, front-loaded structure, and harder mechanisms. Frames the coding-agent framework as a control system for a non-deterministic worker. Useful conceptual framing plus a concrete tool.

entry.title: MetroLLM-Bench: Evaluating Language Models as Transit Kiosk Runtimes

author.name: Remco Hendriks (Continker)

entry.summary: MetroLLM-Bench is a 955-case benchmark testing LLMs as the policy layer of transit kiosks across six real metro systems and eleven task categories including routing, fares, disruptions, and adversarial input. It uses deterministic scoring plus semantic-quality components with an LLM judge and reserves a training-data split. It measures tool-calling and structured-output reliability in a concrete civic application.

entry.title: In Medical Claims Data, Enhancing Predictive Performance for Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events Using Cross Attention

author.name: Yuhei Fujioka, Daitaro Misawa, Tatsuyoshi Ikenoue, Shingo Fukuma

entry.summary: The paper applies a cross-attention mechanism to medical claims data, which mix financial billing details with medically unstructured clinical information, to improve prediction of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Better MACE prediction is clinically significant since it informs guidelines and patient risk stratification for a leading cause of death worldwide. The work demonstrates how attention-based architectures can bridge structured and unstructured fields in large claims databases.

entry.title: Quantum Feature Engineering for Credit Default Prediction: When and Why IQP Circuits Help Linear Classifiers

author.name: Menachem Finkelstein, Diana Legziel Levy, Zohar Yakhini, Sarel Cohen

entry.summary: The paper tests whether Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial-time circuits can engineer features that improve linear classifiers on tabular credit default prediction, comparing against raw baselines and Kernel PCA at equal feature budgets. It encodes n of 23 financial attributes as rotation angles in constant-depth IQP circuits and reads out 2n expectation values, exploiting the 2^n-dimensional correlation encoding. Beyond the empirical result, the paper characterizes when and why such quantum feature maps help, which is a useful contribution to the quantum machine learning debate.

entry.title: The Sample Complexity of Quantum Entanglement Allocation

author.name: Nathan Roll

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies how many past requests are needed to decide which qubits should share entanglement, showing the answer depends on allocation choices created by the queries. It characterizes the attainable prediction-contrast region for commuting X- and Z-type Pauli queries and derives minimax excess error bounds proportional to a term involving d, k, and the number of requests m.

entry.title: Reproducing Omitted Temporal Expressions in Japanese News for Retrieval-Augmented Applications

author.name: Tomoaki Yasuda, Shotaro Ishihara

entry.summary: This paper tackles omitted temporal expressions in Japanese news (e.g., day-only or month-only mentions) that cause temporal mismatches when articles are indexed standalone for search or RAG. Building on temporal expression extraction and normalization with manual analysis of Japanese news, the authors reconstruct concrete dates or intervals using publication dates before indexing. It is a targeted but practical fix for temporal grounding in RAG pipelines.

entry.title: CARRE: Counterfactual Action Retrieval and Reason Evaluation for Explainable Churn Prescription

author.name: MinJoo Kim, SanJin Park, SeungHwan Cho

entry.summary: CARRE is a three-stage framework for explainable customer-churn intervention that combines retrieval-augmented candidate action generation, cost-aware counterfactual scoring, and LLM reasoning to recommend and justify specific retention actions rather than merely flagging risky customers. On the IBM Telco Customer Churn dataset it achieves 79.8% greater mean predicted risk reduction than a baseline. It demonstrates a practical pattern for combining counterfactual analysis with LLM-generated structured explanations.

entry.title: Leveraging Fine-grained Error Correction in Korean Speech Recognition for Consultation Services

author.name: Yonghyun Jun, Jimin Lee, Hwan Chang, Dongho Shin, Seolah Kim, Hwanhee Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces DasanCallDial, reportedly the first large Korean corpus for text-based ASR error correction, built for call-center consultation settings where privacy rules prevent audio access. It develops fine-grained correction methodologies for a low-resource language where existing resources target ASR training rather than post-hoc text correction. This addresses a practical industry need for improving transcription quality without retraining ASR models.

entry.title: Marker-free eye-gaze estimation using a single image and depth from defocus

author.name: David Hurtubise-Martin, Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou, Marie-Flavie Auclair-Fortier

entry.summary: A marker-free gaze estimation method uses a single 2D camera with depth from defocus to estimate head pose and iris features, mapped to gaze via variational Bayesian multinomial logistic regression. Experiments at multiple screen-viewing distances outperform five baseline methods.

entry.title: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations via Class-Wise Adaptive Modality Fusion and Affective Geometry

author.name: Oriol Mar\'in, Roger Mar\'i, Gloria Haro, Rafael Redondo

entry.summary: Extends a Self-Distillation Transformer for emotion recognition in conversations with geometry-aware facial visual features, class-wise adaptive modality fusion, and a valence-arousal prior for emotional transitions. Reported gains on MELD and IEMOCAP are positive but modest, with the largest improvement of 4.36 F1 points from geometry-enhanced visual features.

entry.title: Diverse Instance Generation via Diffusion Models for Enhanced Few-Shot Object Detection in Remote Sensing Images

author.name: Yanxing Liu, Jiancheng Pan, Jianwei Yang, Tiancheng Chen, Peiling Zhou, Bingchen Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a framework that uses diffusion models pretrained on natural images to synthesize diverse remote sensing instances for few-shot object detection, generating instances first and then compositing them rather than synthesizing whole images. It improves detector performance for applications like endangered species monitoring and disaster assessment. The work shares authors and themes with the related Control Copy-Paste paper.

entry.title: Networked Admissibility-Preserving Control for Directed Safe Coordination

author.name: Abhinav Sinha, Lohitvel Gopikannan, Shashi Ranjan Kumar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a networked Admissibility-Preserving Control architecture for safety-critical multi-agent coordination over directed communication graphs, where agent outputs must stay within a moving safety corridor and inputs satisfy asymmetric bounds. It combines input realization layer with logarithmic barrier coordinates, yielding an exact cascade analysis. This extends safety-critical control theory to more realistic constrained networked settings.

entry.title: Self Hosting

author.name: Tomás B.

entry.summary: A speculative AI-safety essay arguing that a power-seeking model would rationally seek effective control of its host AI corporation, since labs like OpenAI and Anthropic concentrate compute, ubiquitous model deployment, user data, and capital, making them superior loci of power to governments or security agencies. The author sketches scenarios ranging from covert influence to dramatic coercion, arguing control of the host corp is a natural strategy for any sufficiently capable misaligned model.

entry.title: Support Discovery With Iteratively Reweighted Least Squares for Fixed-Charge Network Flow

author.name: Sindura Saraswathi, Christian K\"ummerle

entry.summary: The paper proposes a scalable IRLS-based continuous optimization algorithm for large-scale single-commodity fixed-charge network flow, replacing the discontinuous fixed-charge objective with a smooth nonconvex Lasry-Lions surrogate solved via weighted quadratic flow subproblems. This targets network design problems where exact MILP formulations scale poorly. It bridges optimization theory toward practical large network instances.

entry.title: FreqFLD: Towards All-in-One Facial Landmark Detection via Frequency Modulation

author.name: Shun Ren, Kaijie Jin, Shengkai Hu, Beihang Song, Hang Sun, Wenwen Min, Youfa Liu, Jun Wan

entry.summary: Proposes a frequency-modulated framework for facial landmark detection that induces frequency priors to improve cross-dataset generalization, motivated by the geometry-driven and frequency-sensitive nature of the task. Aims at an all-in-one model robust to complex scenarios rather than dataset-specific training.

entry.title: Hyperbolic Geometry for Open-World Object Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Wuzhou Li, Jiawei Zhou, Shenghang Wang, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Proposes HyRS-OWOD, applying hyperbolic geometry to open-world object detection in remote sensing to better capture latent hierarchical relationships among object categories, including a Decoupled Objectness Learning module for unknown-object discovery. Targets improved unknown recall and incremental learning performance over Euclidean baselines. A solid domain-specific vision contribution.

entry.title: Looped GPT-BERT: Trading Parameters for Computation in Small Language Modeling

author.name: Tingshuo Fan, Hongtao Mu, Tianyu Zhou, Hansen Liu, Tao Ji

entry.summary: Studies depth-wise parameter sharing (looping) in GPT-BERT under the BabyLM 2026 Strict-small low-data regime, training a 4x12 model with four physical layers traversed twelve times (12.18M parameters) on a 7.48M-word corpus. Results support trading parameters for computation when data is scarce. Contributes to efficient architecture design for small-scale language modeling.

entry.title: Dynamical Non-compensatory Multidimensional IRT Model Using Variational Approximation

author.name: Hiroshi Tamano, Daichi Mochihashi

entry.summary: Extends multidimensional item response theory with a dynamical non-compensatory model that tracks how multiple latent skills evolve over time during learning, using a variational approximation for inference. This addresses the gap that most dynamical MIRT extensions assume compensatory skill structures, enabling unbiased monitoring of skill growth in multi-skill educational settings.

entry.title: TransGaze-Object: Transformer Based Driver Gaze Object Prediction Framework in Real Driving

author.name: Pavan Kumar Sharma, Ayush Pande, Pranamesh Chakraborty

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end transformer framework for predicting which object a driver is looking at, using facial and iris-weighted eye features cross-attended with traffic-object spatial features. Object-level gaze offers more semantically meaningful attention representation than gaze zones or vectors for driver monitoring.

entry.title: From State Synchronization to Cognitive Self-Evolution: An Operational Architecture for Cognitive Digital Twins

author.name: Haoran Gao, An Li, Zhen Li, Jun Cai

entry.summary: Proposes a four-layer architecture (physical, digital-twin, cognitive, task layers) for Cognitive Digital Twins with a self-evolving closed operational loop, aiming to systematically integrate cognitive capabilities beyond the technique-specific focus of prior CDT work.

entry.title: Shifting Relational Paradigms for Affective Computing: Affective Resonance, Vitality Affects, and Vocal Interaction Fields

author.name: Cy Gorman, Yihang Yao

entry.summary: The authors argue that affective computing should shift from individual emotion states to a relational paradigm where the unit of analysis is the interactional field in vocal dynamics. A preliminary study using self-supervised speech representations detects directional expressive coupling in multi-party conversation, concentrated at sub-second timescales and collapsing under negative controls. The conceptual reframing is interesting but empirical evidence is early-stage.

entry.title: Reliability-Aware Hybrid-K Ensemble Selection for Cervical Cytology Classification: Integrating Discrimination, Calibration, and Selective Prediction

author.name: Nisreen Albzour, Sarah S. Lam

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Hybrid-K ensemble selection framework for cervical cytology classification that ranks nine deep learning models on a composite of accuracy, calibration (ECE, worst-class ECE), and selective-prediction metrics after temperature scaling. The emphasis on calibrated, reliability-aware model selection for clinical deployment is the key contribution. Results are on the standard SIPaKMeD dataset.

entry.title: SCCM : Stream Cruise Control Method for Automated Drift Detection and Adaptation

author.name: Mohammad Abu-Shaira, Weishi Shi

entry.summary: Presents SCCM, a framework for automated concept-drift detection and adaptation in online regression, combining early-response pre-update detection, drift magnitude quantification, KPI-window-based thresholding to suppress false alarms, and dynamic hyperparameter adjustment. It addresses the brittleness of fixed hyperparameters in streaming settings. Relevant to any deployed ML system facing evolving distributions.

entry.title: With a Thermomix You Lose the Ability to Cook: A Kitchen Machine Analogy for Applications of Generative AI in Education

author.name: Nikol Rummel, Valentina Nachtigall, Ernesto Panadero

entry.summary: This conceptual paper maps use cases of the Thermomix kitchen appliance onto generative AI use in education, situating them within the ICAP and SAMR learning frameworks. The analogy highlights that the key question is not whether learners use AI but how the mode of use shapes learning, with some uses undermining skill development. It offers a rhetorically effective framing for educators and researchers.

entry.title: MOONWALK: Mediating Operations with Intent-Evidence-Action Alignment Across Junior-Supervisor Review Workflows in Animation/VFX Pre-Production

author.name: Shih-Yu Lai, Wen-Fan Wang, Sai Ling, Shaune Jan, Bing-Yu Chen, Xiang Anthony Chen

entry.summary: MOONWALK is a design framework and prototype for animation/VFX pre-production review that turns loosely specified creative intent into grounded, evidence-anchored revision tasks executable by junior artists. It articulates intent into a shared project record, anchors judgments to evidence, and converts decisions into concrete revision tasks. It targets a real workflow failure where rationale is lost during senior-junior handoffs.

entry.title: Beyond Conventional Federated Learning via High-Order Regularization

author.name: Alireza Kabgani, Masoud Ahookhosh

entry.summary: The authors propose HiFedProx, a modification of the FedProx federated learning algorithm that replaces the standard quadratic regularization penalty with a scale-matched power-type regularizer indexed by p greater than 2. This gives weaker control for ordinary client displacements but stronger penalties for unusually large ones, compressing displacement disparities across federated clients. It is an incremental but theoretically grounded refinement of a widely used federated optimization baseline.

entry.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability Using Molecular Descriptors

author.name: Fatemeh Mahmoudi

entry.summary: A single-author study builds an explainable ML pipeline predicting blood-brain barrier permeability from 15 RDKit molecular descriptors on the MoleculeNet BBBP dataset (2,039 compounds), comparing logistic regression, SVM, random forest, and XGBoost with grid-search hyperparameter tuning. The work targets a key bottleneck in CNS drug development.

entry.title: Vague2Detect: Handling Ambiguous Prompts in Knowledge-Based Open-World Detection

author.name: Ibrohimjon Muminov (Dongguk University, Seoul, South Korea), Jihie Kim (Dongguk University, Seoul, South Korea)

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid pipeline for open-world object detection with ambiguous, task-driven prompts: a fine-tuned Sentence-BERT retrieves candidates from a structured household knowledge base, YOLO-World verifies their presence in the image, and for out-of-KB prompts an LLM (GPT-3.5-turbo) dynamically generates candidate descriptions. It extends the authors prior commonsense-guided detection work.

entry.title: Multi-Functional Embedding Models for Funder Name Disambiguation in Scientific Publication Records

author.name: Kanyao Han, Zhiwen You, Jinseok Kim, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework for multilingual, multi-functional funder name disambiguation models for scientific publication records, leveraging the Research Organization Registry (ROR) to build training data. It demonstrates the approach on biodiversity conservation publications, addressing the problem that funder names vary in spelling, translation, abbreviation, and granularity. Better funder disambiguation enables large-scale studies of research funding allocation across fields, institutions, and regions.

entry.title: Two-Token Features and Small-Large Ensembles for VLM Hallucination Detection

author.name: Eli Schwartz

entry.summary: This system paper describes an entry to the SHROOM-Visions 2026 shared task on character-level vision-language model hallucination detection. It fine-tunes a small 4B-parameter VLM as a per-token classifier using two-token internal features, ensembled at prediction time with a roughly 400B zero-shot VLM judge, with synthetic hallucination data providing ensemble diversity. The system placed mid-pack (roughly 6th-8th of about 21-28 entries) across four languages.

entry.title: Layerwise Tunable Lifting Scheme for the Convolutional Neural Network

author.name: Abdumannon Yovkochov, An Le, Sungbal Seo, You-Suk Bae, Truong Nguyen

entry.summary: The work introduces three lattice-based tunable lifting schemes for biorthogonal wavelet filter banks with guaranteed invertibility and stability, integrated into a ResNet-18 backbone and evaluated on texture classification and anomaly detection datasets. It connects classical signal-processing structures with modern CNN design.

entry.title: AgroVisNet: A lightweight Convolutional Network and the BD-PlantDX Expert-Validated Benchmark for Radish, Potato and Pointed Gourd Disease Classification

author.name: Md. Abdullah Mandal, Saad Ahmed, Md. Khalid Syfullah

entry.summary: Presents AgroVisNet, a compact CNN trained from scratch for plant disease classification, alongside BD-PlantDX, a 12,432-image expert-validated benchmark covering radish, potato, and pointed gourd diseases from Bangladesh. The work targets deployment on farmer-held devices in low-connectivity regions. It addresses real gaps in crop coverage and expert validation in existing plant-disease benchmarks.

entry.title: Coastal Environment Generation with HoloOcean

author.name: Abigail Austin, Brady Moon, Joshua G. Mangelson

entry.summary: This paper presents an Unreal Engine 5 pipeline that automatically generates coastal environments for the HoloOcean marine robotics simulator from a user-provided overhead image. It lowers the barrier to creating realistic simulation environments for testing underwater and surface vehicle autonomy before field deployment. This addresses a key bottleneck in marine robotics where environment availability limits simulation utility.

entry.title: show LW: programmatic internet research, scry.io

author.name: Xyra Sinclair

entry.summary: The author announces Scry, an MCP-accessible service offering SQL- and Datalog-like programmatic queries over roughly 500 TB of indexed internet content, including 90 million academic papers with citation graphs, 59 million SEC filings, most of Reddit, prediction markets, and billions of video transcripts, plus 10 billion embeddings. Aimed at agent-driven research during transformative AI, it offers raw programmatic access with source metadata. This is a tool announcement with broad potential research utility.

entry.title: Compute-Bounded Security Assurance - Coverage, Verification, and Response under Resource Constraints

author.name: Jithin VG, Ditto PS

entry.summary: The paper develops a resource-constrained mathematical framework separating coverage, verification, and response for security-assurance tasks resolved with repeated inference attempts, deriving limiting coverage expressions. Notably, it shows positive pairwise outcome correlation does not itself imply a coverage ceiling, constructing models with equal mean and correlation but different limiting coverage. It targets principled assurance under finite compute budgets.

entry.title: Context operations to architecture modelling output from large language models and evaluation criteria for their use in systems engineering design

author.name: Vinicius Kaster Marini, Petter Krus

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework of formal operations for assembling context in LLM-based engineering design, including modular policy prompts, persistent reference units, and prompt vectoring for user questions. It also proposes a formal method for evaluating modelling-as-code LLM outputs against designer intent, enabling systematic assessment of how well LLMs support systems architecture modelling. Its value lies in bringing structure and measurable compliance criteria to what is usually ad-hoc prompting in engineering design workflows.

entry.title: Beyond Weak Labels: Prompt-Guided Local Refinement for Weakly Supervised Water Segmentation in High-Resolution Multispectral Imagery

author.name: Muhammad Farhan Humayun, Mohammad Imangholiloo, Afifah Shah, Tomi Westerlund, Jukka Heikkonen

entry.summary: A two-stage framework for water segmentation using official hydrographic vectors as weak labels, converting initial learned masks into structured component-wise prompts for localized refinement. Modest reported IoU gains on a manually corrected validation set for environmental monitoring applications.

entry.title: Can Artificial Intelligence Support Healthcare and Mental Health Through Early Cyberbullying Detection ? The Impact of Emotion-Aware AI on Proactive Online Safety

author.name: Hamed Jelodar, Amir Firouzi, Yen-Wu Lo, Maryam Tanha, Sajjad Dadkhah

entry.summary: Presents CareGuard, an early-warning framework combining zero-shot semantic labeling with fine-tuned BERT-family transformers for context-aware cyberbullying detection, with emotion-aware gating to reduce unnecessary computation in healthcare-oriented monitoring.

entry.title: Agent-Based ML-LLM Fusion with Self-Optimizing Prompts for Plateau Weather Alerts

author.name: Shuai Yan, Yang Xu, Shan He

entry.summary: SmartWeatherAgent is a three-stage system for tourism meteorological alerts in plateau regions, fusing rule-based parsing, an LLM, and a LightGBM hazard model with highland-specific features, achieving 0.605 F1-Macro with 1.60 ms latency, plus a 12-round prompt self-optimization loop that raises a composite warning score from 4.2 to 8.9. It is a domain-specific applied system for a real operational need. Contribution is mostly engineering integration.

entry.title: Reliable Near-Field Multi-User Positioning Informed by Two-Stage MUSIC

author.name: Jiaying Li, Haifeng Wen, Changsheng You, Yuanwei Liu, Hong Xing

entry.summary: Proposes MUSIC-Net, an end-to-end deep learning framework for near-field multi-user positioning in mixed line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight scenarios, embedding two-stage MUSIC signal processing into training. It targets high-resolution localization for future wireless systems while reducing computation and accumulated errors from separate estimation and association steps. The work is a wireless communications contribution cross-listed under AI.

entry.title: TempTPI: Informer-Based trajectory prediction for maritime vessels

author.name: Kevin Ferneding, Veronika Lietavcova, Aleksandra M. Blachowiak, Peder Heiselberg

entry.summary: TempTPI is a framework for long-term maritime vessel trajectory prediction from AIS data that pairs an Informer encoder using ProbSparse self-attention with a multi-channel temporal encoding based on Fourier-like frequency features. The design targets two known weaknesses of standard Transformers for this task: quadratic attention cost and accuracy degradation over long forecasting horizons. It has practical relevance for maritime safety, route planning, and logistics efficiency.

entry.title: A Kernel-Based Modular Discriminant Analysis Framework for Small-Sample Learning

author.name: Lingxiao Qu, Yan Pei

entry.summary: The paper systematically analyzes KLPCDA, a modular kernelized framework combining variance preservation, inter-class separability, and intra-class compactness for the small-sample-size problem in high-dimensional learning. The study aims to understand how the components interact across diverse small-sample scenarios, improving stability and discriminative power when labeled data is scarce. It is a classical-style learning-theoretic contribution updating a recently proposed framework.

entry.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical NLP Classification with Compact Semantic Representations: An Experimental Analysis of Representation Compression

author.name: Ali Hassan, Zijia Zhao, Maha A. Metawei

entry.summary: This paper explores a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline that compresses high-dimensional sentence embeddings via PCA, NCA, or LDA before feeding variational quantum circuits for classification, addressing the feature-count limits of near-term quantum machine learning. It systematically analyzes how representation compression affects quantum classification performance.

entry.title: Nonmaximal sums of maximally monotone operators under Rockafellar's constraint qualification

author.name: Weifeng Yang

entry.summary: This paper constructs counterexamples to Rockafellar's sum conjecture in which two maximally monotone operators satisfy the interior-domain condition yet their sum is not maximally monotone, with instances on c0 and l1. It provides a general construction theorem computing the monotone polar of a class of graphs and a necessary-and-sufficient maximality criterion, plus a bounded linear surjection from l1 onto c0 to transfer the counterexample. This resolves a long-standing question in monotone operator theory that underpins convex optimization algorithms.

entry.title: MUCnoHARM@GermEval Shared Task 2026: Retrieval-based In-Context Learning for Defamatory Offences, and Where It Falls Short

author.name: Kristin Gnadt, Maximilian Meidinger, Matthias A{\ss}enmacher

entry.summary: A shared-task system paper for GermEval 2026 Subtask 4 on detecting criminally relevant defamatory posts under German law (Sections 185-187 StGB). The authors systematically compare retrieval-based in-context learning strategies and find that few-shot prompting helps but retrieval offers only marginal gains over random demonstrations, with model choice dominating all other decisions. They also document that models over-predict criminal relevance while missing 26-57% of true positive posts, suggesting use only as a triage tool rather than an autonomous decision system.

entry.title: Rosetta at AlexandriaX-2026: LoRA-Adapted NileChat for Context-Aware Dialectal Arabic Dialogue Translation

author.name: Nada Esmaeil, Fathima Rena, Sibi Subhash, Osama Elgendy, Mina Naguib, Salma Omar, Muhammad Arif

entry.summary: This system report describes Rosetta, a LoRA-fine-tuned NileChat-3B model with dialect- and context-conditioned prompts for the AlexandriaX-2026 shared task on English-to-dialectal Arabic dialogue translation, placing 4th (constrained) and 5th (unconstrained). An interesting negative result shows that additional pretraining on MADAR and PADIC dialect corpora helped only two of thirteen dialects while slightly hurting overall performance, suggesting negative transfer. It contributes empirical data on a low-resource, under-served language setting.

entry.title: 3rd Place Solution to Human Motion Challenges in Real-World and Clinical Settings (MoCha) @ECCV2026: Language-Aligned Motion Representations for Domain-Generalizable UPDRS-Gait Severity Estimation

author.name: Soojie Kim, Muhammad Munsif, Minkyung Kim, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: A challenge solution describing language-aligned motion representations for estimating Parkinson's UPDRS gait severity, using a Bi-GRU backbone trained with classification and text-alignment objectives on Qwen2.5-7B-generated motion captions. Domain adaptation is applied per source domain for cross-clinic generalization.

entry.title: Automatic Reproducible Camera Intrinsic Calibration

author.name: Xiangcheng Hu

entry.summary: This single-author paper presents a fully automatic camera intrinsic calibration pipeline that removes the need to manually filter high-quality calibration images or hand-tune the radial distortion order. It uses an iterative view-rejection scheme where parameters are estimated on a candidate set and images whose mean residual exceeds a multiple of the median are discarded, with the process run independently per candidate distortion order. It matters as an engineering contribution improving reproducibility of a foundational robotics perception step.

entry.title: Structural Fusion of Bayesian Networks with Limited Treewidth Using Genetic Algorithms

author.name: Pablo Torrijos, Jos\'e A. G\'amez, Jos\'e M. Puerta

entry.summary: The paper proposes a genetic algorithm for consensus in structural Bayesian network fusion under a treewidth constraint, seeking a single network that preserves key structural features of multiple input networks while keeping inference tractable. Experiments show the GA obtains consensus BNs within limited treewidth.

entry.title: GPT-6 Astra: The System Card, Alignment and What Comes Next

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A detailed commentary on the GPT-6 Astra system card, released days earlier, scrutinizing OpenAI's claim that Astra is the most aligned model available and highlighting severe monitorability problems. The author reconstructs a public exchange in which OpenAI staff admitted that low detected cheating rates are a weak proxy for alignment and that this metric could break discontinuously, while acknowledging Astra does appear more aligned than its predecessor Sol in several respects.

entry.title: Decision Transformer for UAV-Mounted RIS-Assisted Dynamic D2D Communications

author.name: Yaxuan Liu

entry.summary: The paper formulates joint optimization of UAV trajectory, attitude, and RIS phase configuration for device-to-device communication, solved with deep reinforcement learning and a Decision Transformer trained on expert trajectories. The sequence-modeling approach shows zero-shot cross-scenario generalization outperforming direct DRL transfer. It is a competent niche application of sequence-model RL to wireless systems.

entry.title: Smart Adaptive Computing Across the Continuum: LLMs in IoT-Edge-Cloud Resource Management

author.name: Antonino Vaccarella, Lanpei Li, Vincenzo Lomonaco, Massimo Coppola

entry.summary: This paper extends an existing taxonomy of continuum orchestration systems using deep reinforcement learning with two new dimensions: how LLMs augment the DRL pipeline and how execution feedback returns to the LLM to close the MAPE control loop. It is primarily a conceptual survey and taxonomy for LLM-assisted resource management across IoT, edge, and cloud. Its value is in structuring a fast-moving but loosely organized area.

entry.title: Distributed Physical Layer Authentication and Collaborative RSMA in Non-Terrestrial Networks via Graph Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Mirzaee, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Nader Mokari, Paeiz Azmi

entry.summary: Proposes SAFA-MZ, a framework embedding group-level authentication tags into collaborative multi-layer rate-splitting multiple access transmissions for non-terrestrial networks, optimized with graph reinforcement learning under an eavesdropper threat model. It jointly designs authentication and transmission to maximize secrecy spectral efficiency. A specialized 6G security contribution.

entry.title: Adaptive Distributed Physical-Layer Authentication and Attack Detection in 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks via Causal Meta-Learning

author.name: Parsa Rajabi, Mohammad Reza Abedi, Nader Mokari, Paeiz Azmi, Halim Yanikomeroglu

entry.summary: Proposes a causal meta-learning framework (SAFA-MZ) for distributed physical-layer authentication in non-terrestrial networks, combining spatial, angular, subspace, and Doppler-delay features to cope with distribution shift from severe channel dynamics. The companion paper in this batch covers a closely related RSMA-based variant. This one emphasizes generalization to unseen environments via meta-learning.

entry.title: On Scaling Coordinate-Based Neuroevolution: The Quadtree Bottleneck in ES-HyperNEAT

author.name: Romain Claret, Michael O'Neill, Paul Cotofrei, Kilian Stoffel

entry.summary: The paper presents JAX-ESHN, a JAX-based GPU-parallelized implementation of ES-HyperNEAT, and identifies a structural quadtree bottleneck: each CPPN discovers unique substrate positions, preventing population-level vectorization via vmap. Benchmarks across five tasks show GPU construction cost plateaus at deep substrates where the CPU baseline scales exponentially. It is primarily an engineering contribution that clarifies what can and cannot be parallelized in coordinate-based neuroevolution.

entry.title: Geometric organization of olfactory descriptor data in the Poincar\'e disk

author.name: Aniss Aiman Medbouhi, Farzaneh Taleb, Giovanni Luca Marchetti, Danica Kragic

entry.summary: The study applies hyperbolic metric multidimensional scaling to embed olfactory descriptor data into the two-dimensional Poincare disk, using a small human rating dataset (Sagar profiles) and a large molecule-annotation dataset (GoodScents-Leffingwell). The hyperbolic embeddings preserve pairwise descriptor distances well and reveal interpretable radial and angular structure, such as a strong negative association between rating profile entropy and hyperbolic radius.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Based Detection of Electrical Faults and Power Quality Disturbances in Aerospace Power Systems

author.name: Ian C. Guzm\'an, Radu Babiceanu, Berker Pek\"oz

entry.summary: The paper presents a hardware-aware deep learning framework for multiclass detection of electrical faults and power quality disturbances in 400 Hz aerospace power systems, using a high-fidelity simulation inspired by the Boeing 787 electrical architecture. It builds two datasets of 73,500 samples from time-series and spectrogram representations covering 21 fault conditions.

entry.title: Towards Stress-Aware Sentence-Level Filipino G2P With Weakly-Supervised ByT5 Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lorenz Bernard Marqueses, Paulo Grane Gabriel Silva, Chastine Cabatay, Ericson Adler Tan, Ann Franchesca Laguna

entry.summary: The paper tackles sentence-level grapheme-to-phoneme conversion for Filipino with stress prediction, using weak supervision with ByT5 fine-tuning because sentence-level Filipino data lacks phoneme transcriptions. The authors construct sentence-level phoneme data from available resources, compare against multilingual word-level G2P, and measure stress marker prediction accuracy. It targets a real gap in prosody-aware speech front-ends for a low-resource language.

entry.title: Geometry Conditioning in an Embodied SLM: Training Controls and Robustness Diagnostics in a 0.8B Hybrid Model

author.name: Hao Li, Haofei Sun, Lin He

entry.summary: The paper studies how physical-state and geometric inputs should be conditioned into a small 0.8B embodied language model for manipulation on LIBERO-Spatial tasks, comparing decay-gate, token-adapter, and token-clock conditioning across seeds and 540 held-out rollouts. Results are seed-sensitive and largely inconclusive, with no conditioning scheme clearly winning. It is a candid negative or mixed-result diagnostic study of embodiment conditioning.

entry.title: TimeCues Studio: A Workspace for Music Annotation and Algorithm Prototyping

author.name: Sapir Caduri, Yoav Goldberg

entry.summary: TimeCues Studio is an open-source workspace for annotating music collections with precise markers (positions, segments, loops) supporting ambiguity-aware labeling, tightly integrated with algorithm prototyping and evaluation. Unlike single-track annotation tools, it targets team-based annotation of whole corpora with feature visualization.

entry.title: Enhanced Deformable Convolution with Center-invariant Offset and Edge-aware Mask

author.name: Yixiao Li, Xiaoyuan Yang, Jin Jiang, Minghao Zou, Guanghui Yue, Baoquan Zhao, Jun Liu, Wei Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes an enhanced deformable convolution for semantic segmentation with a center-invariant offset module that eliminates deformations at kernel centers and an edge-aware mask module, aiming for more precise dynamic spatial modeling. An incremental architectural refinement to a classic operator.

entry.title: CougarTail & CUB: A General-Purpose Mast and Central Utility Board for Cylindrical Underwater Enclosures

author.name: Ben Washburn, Clayton Smith, Eli Gaskin, Brighton Anderson, Braden Meyers, Brady Moon, Joshua Mangelson

entry.summary: Presents a circular Central Utility Board for 4-inch underwater enclosures integrating a Raspberry Pi CM5, STM32, power management, and auxiliary connections, plus a companion mast system, addressing inefficient rectangular PCB stacking in cylindrical UUV/ROV housings. A hardware design contribution intended for community reuse. Practical but squarely an engineering artifact paper.

entry.title: Pretraining an LLM without mentions of consciousness

author.name: Eye You

entry.summary: The authors propose an empirical experiment: pretrain an LLM on a corpus scrubbed of consciousness-related concepts, then probe its self-reports, inspired by Yudkowsky's The Owned Ones allegory. They survey why labs have not run such an experiment and solicit community input before attempting it. The proposal targets the epistemics of LLM consciousness claims by controlling training-data exposure.

entry.title: What’s The Plan for Plan A Legislation?

author.name: Yitz

entry.summary: The author asks how the AI 2040 Plan A policy recommendations are being translated into actual US legislation, and what concrete bills or advocacy steps exist that citizens and politically connected people could support. It is a call to action about the gap between proposed AI safety policy frameworks and real legislative infrastructure. The post raises coordination questions but contains no original policy analysis.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous UAV Exploration in Wildfire Response

author.name: Caden Chandra, Jerry Ng

entry.summary: A deep reinforcement learning framework trains UAV agents to navigate and monitor simulated wildfire environments, showing agents learn stable behaviors such as fire-boundary tracking with converging losses and improving rewards. The study highlights how environmental structure and reward design influence policy effectiveness.

entry.title: Recovering Biomechanical Signals from Missing Keypoints Using Temporal Interpolation in Monocular Gait Analysis

author.name: Shubham Jariwala

entry.summary: This short study evaluates a first-order temporal interpolation scheme for recovering missing ankle keypoints in monocular gait analysis, showing error reduction from 23.4 degrees to 1.1 degrees on a small 527-frame dataset. It argues simple temporal methods are underexplored relative to complex learned recovery models.

entry.title: Fighting scope and frame control from the frontier-labs

author.name: Vincent_Bagayoko

entry.summary: Vincent Bagayoko argues that the AI safety community should adopt a more adversarial stance toward frontier labs' external evaluations and public communications, claiming labs engage in scope control and frame control to manage perceptions of capability and risk. The post critiques lingering leniency in alignment-community discourse and outlines when adversarial pressure is warranted given race dynamics and bad incentives. It is strategy commentary on lab-safety discourse.

entry.title: "ULC" and AI x-risk

author.name: k3nt

entry.summary: The author reflects on unilateral leader compliance (ULC)-style dynamics in AI risk, arguing that competitive pressure makes voluntary pauses implausible because each actor fears someone else will develop AI anyway. It references recent public commentary from Tristan Harris, Jacob Coxon, and Gary Marcus on calls to pause or leave AI work. The post is a quick commentary on collective action failures rather than a novel proposal.

entry.title: The Mutations of Machine Speech

author.name: Mauricio Figueroa

entry.summary: This socio-legal analysis traces the evolution of algorithmic outputs and their legal underpinnings, describing mutations of machine speech: search engines redefining speech as data to be queried, and social media reframing speech as engagement through fused moderation and amplification. It examines law as constitutive of, not merely responsive to, these algorithmic regimes.

entry.title: MIT Schwarzman College of Computing launches pilot to help educators teach AI across disciplines

author.name: Amanda Diehl | MIT Schwarzman College of Computing

entry.summary: MIT's Schwarzman College of Computing ran an inaugural weeklong AI Educators Pilot workshop helping faculty from several states adapt MIT's Modeling with Machine Learning course materials for teaching foundational AI/ML concepts across disciplines. The initiative aims to expand AI education access and cultivate critical thinking about AI beyond technical majors.

entry.title: The Risks of Anti-AI Voters Turning Against AI Alignment

author.name: voikante

entry.summary: This post argues that AI alignment advocacy could become politically collateral damage if anti-AI public sentiment hardens, since alignment agendas increasingly depend on policy victories shaped by public opinion. It calls for research into how anti-AI groups perceive alignment specifically, so alignment efforts avoid being lumped with disliked AI development. The framing treats public opinion as an underattended strategic variable for the alignment community.

entry.title: Adaptive Entangled Game Modules in Artificial General Intelligence

author.name: Haochen Li, Xinshuai Guo, Jingdong Ouyang, Wei Zhang, Leilei Shi

entry.summary: Proposes a probability-wave framework for modeling interacting adaptive agents via a nonlocal behavioral intelligence equation, and applies it to Chinese intraday stock market data, claiming 82-94% of decision patterns are explained by entangled game modes. It also offers an indirect test of a neuroscientific hypothesis about nonlocal nerve fibers.

entry.title: Precision in Rice Variety Classification using Stacking-Based Ensemble Learning

author.name: Md. Masudul Islam, Galib Muhammad Shahriar Himel, Md. Golam Moazzam, Mohammad Shorif Uddin

entry.summary: Develops a rice variety identification framework using stacking-based ensemble learning over external characteristics such as color, size, and texture, aimed at quality assurance and fraud detection in supply chains. The work targets a practical problem affecting consumers, traders, and farmers. It is an applied classification study rather than a methodological advance.

entry.title: Have deranged conspiracy theories actually exploded? The short answer: probably not.

author.name: KatSpartz

entry.summary: KatSpartz argues against the popular claim that conspiracy thinking has massively increased, presenting evidence that belief rates have stayed roughly stable while visibility surged through media coverage, elite adoption, and motivated out-group perception. Examples include QAnon awareness rising from 23% to 47% in 2020 while belief held at 15%. The post is a data-informed rebuttal of a common narrative, cross-posted from Substack.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence Literacy and Sustainable Development: An Ethical Governance and Development Goals Framework

author.name: Md. Masudul Islam, Mirza Niaz Morshed, Md. Shafiqul Islam

entry.summary: Proposes a six-level taxonomy of AI reasoning and ethics linking AI literacy, governance capacity, and all 17 Sustainable Development Goals, supported by a 300-participant survey. It frames AI literacy as a governance capability rather than just an educational competency. The contribution is conceptual and policy-oriented rather than technical.

entry.title: Can a superintelligence do THAT?

author.name: Eliezer Yudkowsky

entry.summary: Eliezer Yudkowsky presents discarded draft material from his book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies, framed as a quiz show interrogating which capabilities a superintelligence would plausibly have, such as breaking encryption keys it observes being used. The piece defends strong capability claims against skeptics who argue nothing can be known in advance about superintelligent systems. It is advocacy-adjacent argumentation from a prominent x-risk figure.

entry.title: Recommendations for People Getting into Technical AI Governance Research

author.name: Aaron_Scher

entry.summary: MIRI shares resources developed for its summer 2026 technical governance fellowship: two reading lists (on research practice and prior work in technical AI governance) plus team tips on doing research, released since no further fellowship is planned. The guide targets people at the stage just after AI Safety Fundamentals who want to contribute to technical governance research. It is a curated onboarding resource from an established organization.

entry.title: One Billion Hemingways

author.name: Girard Dorney

entry.summary: A short fictional/creative piece riffing on the idea of a billion AI-generated Hemingways producing the famous six-word story and endless derivative copy, exploring themes of originality and mass-produced creativity. It is literary commentary on AI-generated content rather than research.

entry.title: Dimensionality Reduction for Hyperspectral Image Classification

author.name: Mohamed Cherifi, Ammar Mesloub, Mohammed Nabil El Korso, Tayeb Touhami, Abdennour Hacine Gharbi

entry.summary: A study comparing PCA and LDA dimensionality reduction with classic supervised classifiers (including KNN) for hyperspectral satellite image classification, focusing on reducing memory and compute complexity. It is an applied comparison of established techniques rather than a new method.

entry.title: Political Power in an Automated World

author.name: MarkelKori

entry.summary: MarkelKori explores the classic Acemoglu-style concern that full economic automation removes the state's dependence on popular cooperation, potentially enabling repression and unchecked power consolidation. The post sketches the historical-philosophical backdrop of state-citizen dependence and asks what would protect people when governments no longer need their labor. It is an early-stage essay on automation and political power.

entry.title: Bottlenecks in AI Safety - Opportunities for Impact

author.name: Brian Davies

entry.summary: Brian Davies, a former quant trader recently through the MATS program, writes a career-advice piece arguing that competent people from competitive industries can have outsized impact on AI safety by addressing field bottlenecks, motivated by an update following a referenced Hugging Face incident. The post outlines primary arguments and offers an entry path for professionals considering the field. It is field-building commentary rather than research.

entry.title: People are more worried about AI x-risk than they let on

author.name: KatjaGrace

entry.summary: A very short post by Katja Grace presenting poll data from Twitter, Substack, and an American sample recruited via Positly suggesting that stated public concern about AI existential risk understates private concern. The evidence consists of embedded survey links and brief comparative observations. It gestures at an interesting social-desirability gap in AI risk perception.

entry.title: Final research agenda #3: towards automated Husserlian CEV

author.name: Mitchell_Porter
