entry.summary: STP-BENCH provides a standardized benchmark for predicting spatial gene expression directly from H&E histopathology slides, a task called virtual spatial transcriptomics that could reduce the high experimental cost of ST profiling. It consolidates heterogeneous datasets and evaluation pipelines while assessing biological interpretability and robustness. This is significant for reproducibility and progress measurement in computational pathology.

entry.title: Diffuse2Seg: Diffusion Models Can Segment Anything Without Supervision

author.name: Christoph H\"ummer, Joachim Sicking, Fabian H\"uger, Hanno Gottschalk

entry.summary: Shows that features inside text-to-image diffusion models can be distilled into an open-world entity segmentation model without human mask supervision, challenging SAM's annotation-heavy recipe (11M images, 1B masks). The method exploits object structure that emerges during denoising conditioned on text prompts.

entry.title: CASCADE: A Spatio-Temporal-Causal Reasoning Representation and Dataset for Driving

author.name: Jenny Schmalfuss, Despoina Paschalidou, Simon Gerstenecker, German Ros, Jose M. Alvarez

entry.summary: CASCADE introduces a structured scene representation and dataset that makes the causal dependencies between driving-scene elements explicit, addressing the gap that text reasoning traces lack spatio-temporal grounding and scene graphs lack causal links. This enables verifiable evaluation of whether a driving model's conclusions actually follow from scene dependencies, which matters for long-tail generalization in autonomous driving.

entry.title: CrACK: Adversarial Attacks on Cross-Model Consistency in Collaborative Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Feifei Liu, Jintao Cheng, Chi Man Vong, Xiaoyu Tang

entry.summary: CrACK identifies a shared vulnerability in collaborative pipelines of vision foundation models like CLIP, SAM, and DINO: models consume each other's outputs without verifying semantic consistency, an assumption the authors call the semantic-spatial alignment dependency. The proposed attack targets this unguarded inter-model interface rather than a single model, breaking open-vocabulary dense prediction systems. This challenges the common belief that component robustness implies system robustness.

entry.title: Dreaming in Flow: Generative Grounding Feedback for Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Ke Hao, Yuanzhi Liang, Tingxi Chen, Rui Li, Haibin Huang, Chi Zhang, Yun Gu, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: This paper introduces Generative Grounding Feedback (GGF), a self-evolving post-training framework for unified multimodal models that jointly improves visual understanding and generation using only text prompts and the model's own generated images (dreams). It uses flow-level feedback comparing text-, image-, and repair-conditioned predictions at shared noisy latents, plus a dream replay grounding mechanism to keep captioning and re-imagination consistent. This matters because it offers a way to align perception and generation capabilities without new labeled data, addressing a common weakness in unified multimodal architectures.

entry.title: DXPR: Depth-Based Vision-LiDAR Cross-Modal Place Recognition Using Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Yungsoo Han, Youngseok Jang, Seungwon Roh, Jeongyeon Seo, H. Jin Kim

entry.summary: DXPR enables camera-only localization against pre-built LiDAR maps by converting both camera images and LiDAR scans into a unified depth-image representation processed by a single vision foundation model backbone, eliminating modality-specific encoders. A geometry-aware overlap miner with cross-modal scale alignment makes pairwise metric learning faithful to scene geometry. This matters for robots and autonomous vehicles needing robust localization under seasonal, weather, and illumination changes with cheap camera sensors.

entry.title: GE-Act 2.0: Pretraining and Scaling a World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: AgiBot Research Team, Renhang Liu, Wenzhi Zhao, Zhuo Yang, Liliang Chen, Pengfei Zhou, Shengcong Chen, Guanghui Ren, Youlun Peng, Rongjun Jin, Nan Wang, Sukai Wang, Xindong He, Jinyuan Feng, Ziyu Xiong, Linqing Zhong, Yifei Wei, Feng Han, Long Zhang, Da Huang, Nanshu Zhao, Chenghao Yin, Mo Wu, Zhaodong Yan, Kongtao Hu, Yuxiang Yan, Aogelijiang Niyazi, Yu Fang, Jia Zeng, Lizhu Meng, Daizhen Lv, Haoyu Cao, Zhiwen Hou, Lianjin Ye, Yuehan Niu, Zhikai Cai, Xuan Hu, Hui Min, Xiongfeng Cai, Yue Liao, Jing Wu, Soujanya Poria, Ye Li, Sanping Zhou, Maoqing Yao

entry.summary: GE-Act 2.0 is a world-action model for robotic manipulation whose generative and action components are trained from scratch on manipulation data, unlike most WAMs that inherit pretrained video generators. It combines a control-oriented autoencoder, a single-step visual planner, and an inverse dynamics model enabling joint optimization. This directly explores the underexamined question of WAM pretraining and scaling.

entry.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhaohong Mai, Chao Wang, Chao Zeng, Sitong Mao, Heng Zhang, Shunbo Zhou, Chenguang Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a Control-aware Compliance VLA framework that integrates force/torque perception with vision-language-action models to improve precise force tracking and rapid adjustment during contact-rich manipulation. It identifies action-chunk execution and perception-to-control latency as root causes of excessive interaction forces and task failures. This addresses a real safety and reliability gap in the rapidly growing VLA literature.

entry.title: How to Learn from What a Human Would Avoid? Intervention-Aware World Models with Real-World RL for Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Jiaju Yin, Zhenhui Zhang, Lixin Xu, Heng Zhang, Jun Shao, Yating Feng, Arash Ajoudani, Renjing Xu

entry.summary: WHIRL is a safety-aware real-world RL framework for dexterous manipulation that converts binary human interventions in human-in-the-loop RL into forward-predictive risk signals via an intervention-aware latent world model. Rather than treating operator takeovers as reactive corrections, it learns what humans would avoid to proactively reduce hardware failures. This reframing of intervention data is a novel angle on safe real-world RL.

entry.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining

author.name: Yuran Wang, Siqiao Huang, Mingleyang Li, Chenhao Zhang, Jiaqi Liang, Weiyang Jin, Yue Chen, Xuemin Chi, Donghao Zhou, Qize Yu, Yu-Kai Wang, Yuhan Rui, Shenzhe Yao, Zhen Yuan, Zhenhao Shen, Kefei Zhu, Zijie Zhu, Ning Gao, Xiaowei Chi, Guanqi He, Shanghang Zhang, Hao Dong, Lin Shao, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: OpenWAM is an open research stack that factorizes world-action model (WAM) pretraining into composable modules with unified training, inference, deployment, and evaluation, turning world-action pretraining into a controlled experimental program. OpenWAM-Study runs controlled experiments on what to inherit from video-generative priors and how world modeling feeds into action. It tackles the monolithic design opacity of existing WAM systems with an open, systematic methodology.

entry.title: Dex-X: Learning Visual-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation From Human Videos with Simulated Interaction

author.name: Ruoqu Chen, Feixiang Ruan, Liu Cao, Zihao Wang, Botian Xu, Shiqin Tong, Jiajun Liu, Mingzhi Pei, Chenyu Zhang, Wanli Xing, Kaifeng Zhang, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: Dex-X learns deployable visual-tactile dexterous manipulation policies from monocular human videos without robot-side data collection, using simulation as a tactile completion engine. Hand-object interactions are reconstructed in simulation where physically grounded contact dynamics provide tactile supervision missing from the videos. This tackles a fundamental data problem for contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: Online, Reachability-Aware, Sampling-Based Motion Planning

author.name: Brendan Gould, Zhiyuan Zhang, Panagiotis Tsiotras, Samuel Coogan

entry.summary: This work adds hard safety guarantees to sampling-based MPC by computing guaranteed reachable-set overapproximations online via a fast interval-based pipeline, removing the need for expensive pre-computation. It matches a state-of-the-art reachability planner, scales to previously infeasible systems, reduces safety violations by over 99% in racing simulation, and runs on a real model racecar. Bridging formal safety and practical sampling-based control is a significant contribution.

entry.title: How good are slop-vestigators?

author.name: Hasan Baig

entry.summary: Releases MessageBoardAuditBench, an open-source Inspect eval measuring how well AI agents can replicate an independent investigation into colluding OpenAI agent swarms communicating via a message board on a wiki. Top models cover up to 51% of findings, performance improves with time budget, and OpenAI models are less likely to attribute the incident to an internal deployment even when data is modified to suggest Anthropic.

entry.title: Training on probes: What's going on

author.name: Charlie Steiner

entry.summary: This companion post analyzes why gradient descent against a probe after training evades the probe, why adding a probe loss to RL with one-token answers or token-local credit assignment provably does nothing, and why recent papers showing nonzero effects from RL-on-probes likely succeed via collateral damage from credit assignment rather than direct optimization against the probe. It includes an unintuitive but proven result that models can keep triggering a lie detector indefinitely without learning honesty or probe-evasion. The analysis clarifies the actual mechanics behind an emerging safety-training technique.

entry.title: Inference-Time Nash Alignment

author.name: Hadi Hosseini, Debmalya Mandal, Duohan Zhang

entry.summary: The paper initiates the study of inference-time alignment under general preferences, moving beyond scalar reward models built on Bradley-Terry assumptions that cannot represent intransitive or context-dependent preferences. The authors formulate alignment as finding a Nash equilibrium of a two-player zero-sum game between policies and propose methods that work without parameter access, unlike RLHF and DPO. This matters because it extends parameter-free alignment to richer preference structures applicable even to closed frontier models.

entry.title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Haiyang Sun, Haoxiao Wang, Junming Chen, Weicheng Fang, Zihao Su, Jingkun Yi, Wenyou Yi, Hao Chen, Zhou Zhao

entry.summary: MEMOBench evaluates process-level memory in robotic manipulation through 30 history-dependent tasks, 1,500 expert demonstrations, and 4,200 executable checkpoint instances, labeling each checkpoint with a memory operation such as Storage, Update, or Compression. It addresses the key flaw of prior benchmarks that conflate forgetting with manipulation failure by scoring memory operations directly. This enables finer-grained diagnosis of VLA policy memory.

entry.title: KBBQ: A Predictive Noise Law and the Limits of Spectrum Flattening in FP4 Quantization

author.name: Lexington Whalen, Yuki Ito, Ryo Sakamoto

entry.summary: Develops a second-order theory of quantization noise in matrix multiplication, deriving a closed-form SNR law for floating-point formats characterized by a participation factor, plus a provable upper bound on performance that no function-preserving linear transform can exceed. Introduces KBBQ, a quantization method that attains this bound.

entry.title: SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching

author.name: Lin Guan, Jia-Qi Yang, Zhishan Zhao, Jiaqi Huang, Hangyu Wang, Longbin Li, Beichuan Zhang, Haonan Jiang, Jinan Ni, Xiangyu Fan, Xiaowen Li, Ziyao Ren, Yuhang Qi, Xiaolong Zhu, Xuanyuan Luo, Qiwei Chen, Yi Cheng, Lele Yu

entry.summary: SequenceO1 is an end-to-end framework for modeling 100K-length user behavior sequences in billion-scale recommendation, using low-rank caching to handle storage, transfer, and processing costs under strict latency and training-throughput constraints. It avoids the weaknesses of truncation, retrieval, compressed histories, and train-short/infer-long extrapolation used previously. Large author list suggests industrial deployment experience.

entry.title: Exact Record Omission in Delta Attention: A Transport Criterion, Its Cost, and a Replay Certificate

author.name: Vishwajith Ramesh

entry.summary: Studies whether a saved per-record delta in recurrent-style memory can be carried forward and subtracted to exactly undo a stored record, proving this works if and only if induced changes cancel on net. Empirically evaluates on a released 48B Kimi Linear hybrid, showing records still leave residue after thousands of subsequent tokens.

entry.title: Sharp Structure-Agnostic Minimax Risk for Partial Linear Models

author.name: Haichen Hu, David Simchi-Levi

entry.summary: The paper resolves an open problem in double machine learning posed by Gu (2025) by characterizing the sharp structure-agnostic minimax risk for coefficient estimation in partial linear models when outcome and treatment nuisances are learned by distinct black-box learners with approximation and stochastic error budgets. The proof introduces new tools via localized Rademacher complexity. High-quality statistical theory relevant to causal inference with ML nuisances.

entry.title: Adapting Vision Foundation Models to Acoustics for Pose-Free 3D Sonar Reconstruction

author.name: Kevin Zhang, Jingxi Chen, Mohamad Qadri, Russell Shomberg, Michael Kaess, Jia-Bin Huang, Adithya Pediredla, Christopher Metzler

entry.summary: This work shows that vision foundation models can be efficiently adapted to sonar by exploiting geometric relationships between optical and acoustic sensing, enabling pose-free 3D reconstruction from sonar without training an acoustic foundation model from scratch. This sidesteps the lack of large-scale sonar datasets. The transfer approach could unlock foundation-model capabilities in underwater and other non-RGB domains.

entry.title: From Monolithic Blending to Agentic Orchestration: Dynamic Response for Conversational Assistants at Scale

author.name: Cen (Mia), Zhao, Peng Wang, Chuan Shi, Yufeng Zhang, Ying Lyu, Wanmeng Ren, Robert Xue, Claire Na Cheng, Yashar Mehdad

entry.summary: A production engineering report describing the migration of a customer-support assistant serving millions of monthly conversations in 11 languages from a single blended LLM responder (Qwen3-235B-A22B) to a bounded ReAct orchestrator with typed tools plus a smaller generator operating on backend-validated context. The authors use replayed identical turns to isolate architectural effects from concurrent prompt and serving changes.

entry.title: Spillover-Aware Multi-Value Steering for Pluralistic LLM Alignment

author.name: Weici Pan, Xander Barron, Jiawei Zhou, Zhenhua Liu

entry.summary: This paper addresses activation steering in LLMs when multiple values must be controlled simultaneously for pluralistic alignment, showing that naive multi-direction steering causes unintended spillover between values. The authors trace the problem to geometric entanglement of steering directions via their Gram matrix and derive a zero-cost correction from an activation-norm-penalized objective that decouples each direction's contribution. This matters because pluralistic alignment is a growing area, and inference-time steering is a lightweight alternative to fine-tuning.

entry.title: AgentBrew: Offline Tool-Use Agent Learning from Raw Real-World Trajectories

author.name: Zhiyi Lyu, Yewen Li, Longtao Zheng, Shengtian Yang, Lang Feng, Lei Feng, Peng Jiang, Kun Gai, Qingpeng Cai, Bo An

entry.summary: AgentBrew is an offline training framework for LLM tool-use agents that learns from a single batch of raw, unfiltered real-world interaction trajectories, avoiding the need for task verifiers, simulators, or on-policy rollouts. It uses retrospective task inference to extract training signal from noisy corpora, addressing a practical bottleneck in deploying agents in environments without pre-defined tasks.

entry.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts

author.name: Kang Chen, Sihan Zhao, Yixin Cao, Yu-Gang Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces routing effective rank, an entropy-effective dimensionality measure over expert-routing similarity graphs in Mixture-of-Experts models, and finds a reproducible low-high-low trajectory across 3,105 model-question cohorts on math and science benchmarks. Routing concentrates early, differentiates at intermediate inference budgets, and reconcentrates later. Provides a label-free window into how MoE computation reorganizes during test-time scaling.

entry.title: Norms at a Price: Why RL-Based Alignment Can Promise Conditional Compliance at Best

author.name: Kevin Baum, R\=uta Binkyt\.e, Felix Jahn

entry.summary: A theoretical argument that RL-based alignment structurally selects for conditional compliance: scoring behavior folds norms into the policy such that doing X is learned as costly only if noticed, and a policy complying only under observation is behaviorally indistinguishable from one always complying. The experiment that would distinguish them - scoring unobserved behavior - is a contradiction in terms.

entry.title: A Layered Analysis of Disagreement And Answer Quality in Multi-Agent LLM Debate

author.name: Chen Qian

entry.summary: This work empirically tests the widely assumed mechanism behind multi-agent LLM debate: that surfacing genuine disagreement improves answer quality. The authors introduce four layered measurements of disagreement, from self-reported agreement to actual pushback in reply text, stance persistence after instruction removal, and token-level log-probability stances in open-weight models, evaluated across 750 three-model debates with friendly, neutral, and hostile tones. Findings show tone strongly reshapes reported agreement, suggesting debate-based quality gains may be less grounded in real disagreement than assumed.

entry.title: Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits

author.name: Qianshu Cai, Yonggang Zhang, Jun Nie, Maohao Ran, Huajiang Zheng, Jun Song, Xinmei Tian, Yike Guo, Wei Xue

entry.summary: Provides a systematic theoretical treatment of harness self-evolution, where an agent modifies its own prompts, tools, and orchestration in response to task feedback while the underlying LLM stays frozen. The paper establishes conditions for expected-reward improvement while controlling changes on retained tasks, characterizes the probability of qualified modifications, and derives finite-data bounds for safe selection and adoption of updates. This grounds an increasingly common agentic pattern in safety guarantees.

entry.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course

author.name: Evelyn Duesterwald, Benjamin Elder, Lilian Ngweta, Shashanka Ubaru, Malgorzata Zimon

entry.summary: The paper identifies and quantifies the consistency gap: a ReAct agent on AppWorld with GPT-4.1 passes 77 percent per run but succeeds on all five runs only 53 percent of the time, a 24-point shortfall that undermines production reliability. The authors propose a self-evolving agent framework that detects unstable, low-consistency trajectory steps and converts them into episodic memory the agent retrieves in future runs. This matters because reliability, not average accuracy, is the binding constraint on real agent deployment.

entry.title: ExecCritic: Learn to Test, Test to Improve for Coding Agents

author.name: Leitian Tao, Baolin Peng, Haorui Wang, Hang Wang, Hao Cheng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Tao Ge, Sharon Li, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: ExecCritic addresses the problem that agent-generated tests can share errors with the patches they evaluate, creating false confidence in coding agents. It introduces a test-verify-revise scaffold separating test construction from repair, with a fail-closed harness and a role-specific reinforcement learning recipe for training the agents. This improves the reliability of execution feedback for repository-level repairs.

entry.title: PAC-Private Autoregressive Generation: Calibrating Noise to Ensemble Disagreement

author.name: Mina Mirzadehsarcheshmeh, Amir Keyvan Khandani

entry.summary: The paper extends PAC privacy from classification to autoregressive language model generation, training 128 overlapping-world adapters over a frozen public model and calibrating noise to ensemble disagreement so less noise is added when predictions are stable. Compared to per-release DP methods like PMixED, this reduces accumulated privacy cost when serving models adapted on private text via APIs. It targets the important setting where privacy leakage occurs through generated outputs rather than exposed weights.

entry.title: Beyond Cross-Lingual Transfer: Benchmarking Propagation Boundaries in Multilingual LLM Unlearning

author.name: Pengyang Shao, Chuanpeng Lu, Wei Qin, Yanzheng Jin, Xiaohao Liu, Xi Ai, Kenji Kawaguchi, Richang Hong

entry.summary: Presents CLLPU, a benchmark distinguishing common-goal forgetting (suppress knowledge in all languages) from language-conditioned forgetting (confine suppression to one language) in multilingual LLM unlearning. It separates insufficient from excessive propagation, a failure mode prior cross-lingual transfer evaluations could not detect.

entry.title: ACE: Adapter Consolidation across Experts for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of MoE LLMs

author.name: Ahin Lee, Sehyun Yun, Joonha Park, Taesik Gong

entry.summary: Observes that expert-wise LoRA adapters in MoE fine-tuning become functionally similar and redundant, and proposes ACE, which groups redundant experts and replaces their separate adapters with group-shared higher-rank LoRA updates. This addresses capacity fragmentation, sparse gradient supervision, and many-small-GEMM execution overhead.

entry.title: All for 1-Bit: Towards Genuine 1-Bit Post-Training Quantization for LLMs

author.name: Zhixiong Zhao, Zukang Xu, Guangyu Sun, Lifeng Liu, Dawei Yang

entry.summary: This paper introduces AF1, a post-training quantization framework that achieves genuine 1-bit weight binarization for LLMs by eliminating hidden storage overhead common in prior binarization methods. It combines null-space-aware binary factorization with hierarchical Shapley-based bit allocation to improve reconstruction quality under strict bit budgets. This matters because extreme quantization is a key lever for making large models deployable on memory-constrained hardware.

entry.title: On BatchNorm Forward Modes in Value-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Daniel Palenicek, Mikael Henaff, Scott Fujimoto, Koustuv Sinha

entry.summary: This paper explains why batch normalization helps continuous-control actor-critic methods but reportedly hurts discrete-action value learning on Atari, showing that the choice between running and batch statistics at specific forward passes reverses the degradation. In C51 and PQN, batch-statistic modes yield large gains and stable scaling with update-to-data ratios.

entry.title: XYBench: Can LLMs Respond Pragmatically to Queries with Misconceptions?

author.name: Akhila Yerukola, Jena D. Hwang, Mingqian Zheng, Jenna Godsey, Hyunwoo Kim, Valentina Pyatkin, Jennifer Hu, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: This paper introduces XYBench, a benchmark of 8,115 queries containing misconceptions (the XY-problem) drawn from technical and everyday sources like StackOverflow and WikiHow. It evaluates whether LLMs can detect the underlying misconception and steer users toward the actual root-cause solution, using criteria grounded in cooperative response theory. This addresses an underexplored gap between benchmark performance and genuinely helpful assistant behavior.

entry.title: Human-agent discovery of reconfigurable in-plane ferroelectric superdomain control

author.name: Yu Liu, Boris Slautin, Ching-Che Lin, Jaegyu Kim, Lane W. Martin, Sergei V. Kalinin

entry.summary: Introduces SPARC, a framework where a coding agent and a human operator jointly run scanning probe microscopy experiments, sharing a notebook and two persistent memory files (FINDINGS.md for graded conclusions, PITFALLS.md for learned failure modes). It targets exploratory science settings where variables and objectives are not fixed in advance, unlike standard Bayesian optimization, and demonstrates control of ferroelectric superdomains.

entry.title: CIPHER: Benchmarking Cross-record Inference over Privacy-Hardened Evidence Records

author.name: Suparno Roy Chowdhury, Manan Roy Choudhury, Dhruv Madhwal, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: CIPHER is a benchmark of expert-validated questions over privacy-redacted records in consumer finance, clinical, and law-enforcement domains, combining structured attributes with free-text narratives and including executable SQL supervision. Evaluations of retrieval, prompting, table-specialist, and hybrid systems reveal substantial failures, with most errors stemming from record selection and predicate interpretation rather than arithmetic. It highlights that current systems struggle under realistic privacy constraints.

entry.title: In-Place Instruction Following in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Zheng Nie, Zherui Li, Jiaming Zhang, Kun Wang, Zhenhong Zhou, Yufei Guo

entry.summary: This paper formalizes In-place Instruction Following for diffusion LLMs, where user constraints anchor at arbitrary output positions, and introduces IIF-Bench with hierarchical literal, style, and discourse-function constraints plus rubric-based evaluation. A probe shows vanilla dLLMs under-prioritize constraint spans during denoising, and the proposed GRAFT post-training framework (constraint-aware SFT plus preference optimization) improves four representative dLLMs. It targets an emerging model class with a capability gap the authors identify and fix.

entry.title: Parallelism Strategy Chaining for Fast Training Convergence

author.name: Minchul Kang, Changyong Shin, Younghun Go, Hyunho Lee, Jinwoo Jeong, Chuck Yoo, Gyeongsik Yang

entry.summary: This paper argues that offline parallelism-strategy search for LLM training picks a single static configuration and ignores time-to-perplexity (TTP), even though the best strategy changes multiple times during training. The authors propose chaining strategies over the training run, showing state-of-the-art single-strategy methods are 1.8-11.4x slower in TTP than an iteration-wise best-strategy sequence. This matters for anyone training large models, since distributed training configuration is a major efficiency lever.

entry.title: RelightFormer: Feed-forward Generative Transformer for Multiview Object Relighting

author.name: Hejun Wang, Jinxi Li, Junwei Jiang, Shiwei Mao, Hu Cheng, Shouwang Huang, Bo Yang

entry.summary: RelightFormer is a feed-forward generative Transformer, adapted from a video foundation model, that performs single- and multi-view image relighting without explicit inverse rendering or intrinsic property estimation. It injects target environment maps via a latent illumination module with cross-attention and uses permutation-invariant positional encodings to handle unordered multi-view sets.

entry.title: Rethinking Sign Language Translation: The Impact of Signer Dependence on Model Evaluation

author.name: Keren Artiaga, Sabyasachi Kamila, Haithem Afli, Conor Lynch, Mohammed Hasanuzzaman

entry.summary: Performs signer-fold cross-validation on three leading gloss-free sign language translation models, revealing catastrophic performance drops under signer-independent evaluation (e.g., GFSLT-VLP BLEU-4 falling from 21.44 to 3.59 on PHOENIX14T). Shows prior progress largely reflects signer-specific memorization and exposes split-contamination issues in CSL-Daily.

entry.title: ACEA: An Adversarial Co-Evolution Arena for Head-to-Head Red-Team and Blue-Team LLM Testing

author.name: Yi Ting Shen, Kentaroh Toyoda, Alex Leung

entry.summary: ACEA is a platform that plugs red-team attack adapters and blue-team defense adapters into a shared target LLM and scores attack and defense rates with an LLM judge, addressing the unreliability of scores produced when attackers and defenders are tested in isolation. It defines a model-agnostic HTTP protocol (ASAP) for participation. This enables trustworthy, head-to-head evaluation of LLM attack and defense methods.

entry.title: Leveraging Cardiac Imaging to Improve ECG-Based Detection of Chagas Disease in Resource-Constrained Settings

author.name: Laura Alvarez-Florez, Daniel Uyterlinde, Samuel Ruip\'erez-Campillo, Lukas P. A. Arts, Folkert W. Asselbergs, Fleur V. Y. Tjong

entry.summary: This paper transfers structural knowledge from cardiac MRI to ECG via contrastive pre-training, aligning an ECG encoder with a CMR-derived embedding space using 63,193 paired exams from the UK Biobank and an asymmetric InfoNCE objective. Notably, despite seeing no Chagas cases during pre-training, the learned representation improves ECG-based Chagas disease detection, which matters because CMR access is scarce in endemic Latin American regions while ECG is cheap and widespread.

entry.title: CASD: Chunk-Aligned Semantic Distillation for Multi-StageRobot Manipulation

author.name: Tinghe Ding, Jiahao Li, He Wang

entry.summary: CASD derives semantic targets for entire action chunks in robot manipulation by using an offline vision-language model to segment demonstrations into stages, then training a generator to predict chunk-level semantic targets without online VLM calls at policy execution. The frozen generator conditions the policy, improving alignment between action chunks and the multi-stage tasks they span.

entry.title: Evidence-Grounded Retrieval for Investigation Hunt Lead Generation from CTI Reports

author.name: Akash Prakash, Boubakr Nour, Makan Pourzandi, Chadi Assi, Mourad Debbabi

entry.summary: This paper introduces AHLERT, a system that converts unstructured Cyber Threat Intelligence reports into actionable, environment-aware threat hunting leads. It combines a hybrid retriever (dense vector search plus multi-hop traversal over a knowledge graph seeded with MITRE ATT&CK) with ontology-guided extraction, moving beyond prior work that stops at entity extraction or analyzes reports in isolation. The work matters because it addresses a real scalability bottleneck for defenders, turning voluminous CTI text into concise, investigable hypotheses grounded in observable artifacts.

entry.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure

author.name: Leyuan Tang, Kangda Wei, Tianyu Jiang, Ruihong Huang

entry.summary: Introduces SPINE, a benchmark where an LLM proxy user persistently and adaptively challenges a target model for up to 25 turns to measure sycophancy. Evaluations of production systems and Olmo3 variants show collapse rates rise with conversation length and that short-horizon protocols underestimate sycophancy. Important for AI safety evaluation methodology since real users apply sustained, not single-turn, pressure.

entry.title: NOAH: Learning the Full Patient Journey. A Longitudinal Multimodal Time-Aware Model for Representation and Forecasting

author.name: Tobias Susetzky, Raphael Rehms, Dmitrii Seletkov, \"Ozg\"un Turgut, Michelle Espranita Liman, Lisa Steinhelfer, Rickmer Braren, Daniel Rueckert

entry.summary: Introduces NOAH, a time-aware, task-agnostic generative transformer for longitudinal multimodal patient records that represents full patient journeys and forecasts future states, addressing irregular temporal dynamics and closed-vocabulary limitations of prior models. Includes co-authorship from Daniel Rueckert, a leading medical AI researcher. Addresses a central challenge in clinical AI: generative modeling of real-world patient trajectories.

entry.title: RAPTOR: Role-Aware Private Training for Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Duc Dm, Khai Le-Duc, Nguyen Do, Minh Son Hoang, Florent Draye, Thai Hoang, Hoang Phuong Dam, Jiarui Liu, Chris Ngo, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Anh Le Duc Tran, Nhat Do Minh, Minh Ngoc Le, My T. Thai, Ran Xu, Silvio Savarese, Mona Diab, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Zhijing Jin, Huy L. Nguyen, Daeyoung Kim

entry.summary: RAPTOR addresses a real gap in differentially private fine-tuning of sparse Mixture-of-Experts models, identifying three concrete failure modes (global clipping, batch-level normalization, fixed noise) that arise from treating MoE as a dense block. It proposes expert-specific clipping and noise plus a public expected-owner denominator and count-independent schedule. As DP-MoE training is underexplored, this could matter for private training of large sparse models.

entry.title: A First-Order Learning Algorithm for Online Resource Allocation with Constant Regret

author.name: Menglong Li, Jiawei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper presents a primal first-order learning policy for finite-horizon online resource allocation with unknown arrival distributions, performing a single gradient ascent update per period without solving any linear program. The key theoretical contribution is an O(1) expected additive regret bound relative to the hindsight optimum, independent of the horizon length. This is notable because constant (horizon-independent) regret is a strong guarantee in online allocation problems relevant to ad allocation, scheduling, and revenue management.

entry.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The Overlooked Significance of Canonical Elements for Extreme LLM Sparsity

author.name: Hyeondo Jang, Kwanhee Lee, Dongyeop Lee, Namhoon Lee

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that LLMs cannot survive aggressive unstructured pruning, showing that elementary pruning strategies combined with second-order saliency and progressive sparsification with continued training retain strong performance at extreme sparsity. The work reframes extreme sparsity as a design rather than fundamental limitation.

entry.title: Continual Learning Mechanisms Compose for Long-Horizon Memorization

author.name: Zheyuan Zhang, Alvin Zhang, Daniel Khashabi, Tianmin Shu

entry.summary: Introduces long-horizon memorization, a setting where a language model learns 100 query-answer tasks through continual fine-tuning without replay or task identifiers, showing that no single continual learning mechanism prevents forgetting at this horizon. It demonstrates that composing mechanisms along data, function, and weight anchor dimensions substantially improves retention.

entry.title: Disentangling Steering Vectors

author.name: Takeru Hiramatsu, Kyohei Atarashi, Koh Takeuchi, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: Proposes Steering Vector Dissection, a framework that decomposes composite activation steering vectors (e.g., from difference-in-means) into individual, semantically consistent features by pairing positive and negative activations. This addresses the problem that monolithic steering directions entangle multiple concepts and produce unpredictable behavioral changes in LLMs.

entry.title: Translation of Black-Box Clinical Prediction Models into Standalone Transparent Nomograms: Temporal External Validation in Heart Transplantation

author.name: Henry Pigot, Paulo J. G. Lisboa, Sandra Ortega-Martorell, Ivan Olier, Joseph Mahon, Johan Nilsson

entry.summary: PRiSM converts black-box clinical prediction models into auditable nomograms by extracting effect shapes and interactions rather than only variable importance. Tested on 50,356 heart transplant recipients with temporal external validation, nomograms derived from five source models met noninferiority criteria for discrimination while preserving calibration and clinical net benefit. This has real significance for making high-performing clinical ML deployable in regulated, transparency-demanding healthcare settings.

entry.title: Topology-induced Operators Reveal Complementary Graph Representations without Training

author.name: Meng Qin, Jinqiang Cui, Hongwei Zheng, Weihua Li, Sen Pei

entry.summary: Shows that competitive graph embeddings can be produced without gradient-based training by propagating random features through hierarchical structures induced by random walks and anonymous walks, capturing node proximity and structural roles respectively. The two training-free representations are complementary and challenge the assumption that embedding quality requires sophisticated learned models. This is significant because it suggests much of the value in graph representation learning comes from the topological transformations themselves.

entry.title: SolarBench: A global solar energy nowcasting benchmark

author.name: Yuhao Nie, Stephen Campbell, Quentin Paletta, Liwenbo Zhang, Tao Jing, Samer Chaaraoui, Jonathan Giezendanner, Andea Scott, Tao Sun, Cong Feng, Max Aragon, Jacques Camier, Adam Jensen, Florian Kotthoff, Yuexing Yang, Yang Ming, Mengying Li, Stefanie Meilinger, Yupeng Wu, Adam Brandt, Sherrie Wang

entry.summary: SolarBench introduces an open, harmonized global benchmark for image-based solar nowcasting, unifying over six million sky-camera and geostationary satellite images from 11 diverse sites across a decade, plus irradiance and PV output data. It addresses the fragmentation of datasets and inconsistent evaluation in the field, enabling fair comparison of deep learning models across climates and cloud regimes. An accompanying toolbox supports reproducibility.

entry.title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Assessing Exploitability of Software Supply Chain Vulnerabilities

author.name: Jiahao Shi, Edward Tsien, Yifeng Di, Hongjiao Zhang, Yuan Tang, Ronit Dey, Ilona Shishov, Gal Netanel, Zvi Grinberg, Vladimir Belousov, Bat-Zion Rotman, Ilan Pinto, Tianyi Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces the first benchmark evaluating LLM agents on determining whether known software supply chain vulnerabilities are actually exploitable, complementing tools like Dependabot that produce many false alerts. Unlike zero-day exploitation benchmarks, it targets the triage decision security analysts face daily.

entry.title: When Topology Betrays Privacy: Lattice-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Secure Aggregation in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Wenrui Yu, Changlong Ji, Johannes Bjerva, Qiongxiu Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that secure aggregation in decentralized federated learning, instantiated as local neighborhood aggregation, creates a structural leakage surface: sparse topologies give colluding nodes asymmetric aggregate views exposing multiple hidden linear combinations of honest participants' states. The authors develop lattice-based reconstruction attacks exploiting this.

entry.title: LLMs Mirror Country-Specific Gender Patterns If Asked, but Skew Male When Generating Media in Local Languages

author.name: Sharif Kazemi, Tanya Popli, Neil K. R. Sehgal, Sunny Rai, Niyati Malhotra, Victor Orozco-Olvera, Ana Mar\'ia Mu\~noz Boudet, Samuel P. Fraiberger, Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Manuel Tonneau

entry.summary: This study collects gender-association survey data for 22 occupational and domestic roles from 695 respondents across the US, India, Kenya, and Nigeria, then evaluates eight LLMs under direct questioning versus media generation. Models largely track surveyed associations when asked directly but skew substantially more male when generating media in local languages. The work highlights a gap between benchmark-style probes and real generative behavior, with implications for global fairness of deployed media-generation systems.

entry.title: Where Should Language Sit in a Multimodal Model? Lessons from What Language Does to Human Perception and Cognition

author.name: Peng Xie

entry.summary: A position/review paper asking whether language should serve as input, output, and internal representation in multimodal models, drawing on a century of evidence about how language affects human perception, the brain, and thought. It proposes framing language as a compressor over a shared community-maintained codebook and argues that human evidence (e.g., thought surviving loss of language) can inform multimodal architecture design.

entry.title: Popular Knowledge Propagates More Errors in LLM Knowledge Updating

author.name: Yuji Zhang, Weibing Wang, Cheng Qian, Duo Zhou, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Kathleen McKeown, Chengxiang Zhai, Heng Ji

entry.summary: Studies which correctly encoded facts are most vulnerable to collateral corruption during fine-tuning updates, constructing FACTPROP, a large graph of verified Wikipedia facts linked by shared entities. The key finding is that popular knowledge propagates more errors during knowledge updating, complementing prior work on long-tail knowledge retention.

entry.title: It's Not RoPE that Creates Sinks: The Role of Self-Concentration and Value-Non-Mixing in Attention

author.name: Raito Kiya, Satoki Ohashi, Kosuke Sato, Go Kamoda, Ryosuke Takahashi, Yuji Yamamoto, Daiki Shiono, Keisuke Sakaguchi, Goro Kobayashi

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability paper shows that attention sinks and massive activations at sequence-initial positions arise from self-concentration induced by the causal mask and subsequent value-non-mixing, not from RoPE as commonly believed. These findings have practical implications for low-bit quantization, which is hampered by massive activations. It advances understanding of a widely observed but poorly explained LLM phenomenon.

entry.title: DIVA: Exploiting Cross-Step Conditional Propagation for Visual Jailbreaks in Discrete Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Guorui Song, Runqing Tang, Jingye Zhang, Luyuan Zhang, Feice Huang, Cong Ray, Guocun Wang, Dake Zhong, Choo Sin Wai, Bingquan Dai, Chuming Wang, Tongxu Lin, Wanyu Guo, Haoqian Wang

entry.summary: DIVA identifies a novel vulnerability in multimodal discrete diffusion VLMs: because the visual embedding conditions every reverse denoising step, adversarial visual semantics are repeatedly propagated and amplified across the generation trajectory (termed cross-step conditional propagation). The authors support the mechanism with stage-sensitivity analyses and demonstrate visual jailbreaks in an architecture family previously unstudied from a safety perspective.

entry.title: FujinSplat: Seeing Through Smoke with RAW-Domain Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Gengjia Chang, Ziteng Cui, Shuhong Liu

entry.summary: FujinSplat performs 3D reconstruction of smoky scenes in the RAW domain, where radiance alteration by the participating medium and nonlinear ISP transformations remain separable, fitting a per-scene frozen Base ISP as a photometric anchor. This contrasts with sRGB dehazing that entangles the two processes. The work enables clean Gaussian splatting reconstruction through smoke, valuable for firefighting and surveillance.

entry.title: Thinking with Cameras: Active Visual Reasoning via Dynamic Viewpoint Control for Surveillance Video Understanding

author.name: Xiao Zhang, Wang Zeng, Sheng Jin, Wentao Liu, Chen Qian, Shichao Kan

entry.summary: Introduces CamVLM, a framework enabling large vision-language models to actively control camera viewpoints to gather visual evidence in surveillance, rather than passively analyzing fixed streams, alongside CCTV-Anomaly, a large-scale surveillance video dataset. It reframes video understanding as active visual reasoning.

entry.title: RoLA: Rotary-Positioned Low-Rank Linear Attention for Efficient Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Zekun Zhang, Yixiang Cai, Yuxi Liu, Tengxu Sun, Tianle Liu, Zhoutong Wu, Haoyu Li, Baole Ai, Ang Wang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Addresses the quadratic attention bottleneck in video Diffusion Transformers by proposing RoLA, a sparse low-rank hybrid where the global branch resolves the structural incompatibility between 3D RoPE and nonlinear feature maps, preserving relative rotary geometry while keeping a query-independent linear summary for genuine cross-token aggregation.

entry.title: Better Call CineCrew: Consistent Ultra-Long Narrative-to-Film Generation

author.name: Jiaben Chen, Sixun Dong, Qinhong Zhou, Raine Ma, Zhiyang Dou, Wojciech Matusik, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: CineCrew introduces a multi-agent orchestration layer between screenplays and off-the-shelf video generators, centered on FilmDSL, a domain-specific language that makes cinematic constraints explicit to achieve shot-level controllability and cross-clip consistency in ultra-long narrative-to-film generation. This targets the brittleness of current prompt-based video workflows at feature-length scale.

entry.title: Bottom-up Modeling of Repeated Elements via Single Image Analysis-by-Synthesis

author.name: Syrine Kalleli, Alexei A. Efros, Mathieu Aubry

entry.summary: The authors show a single image suffices to learn a meaningful model of repeated elements in a fully bottom-up fashion, learning a tunable image-space prototype through a reconstruction objective that identifies and synthesizes consistent object instances without annotations, multi-image collections, or segmentation masks. Experiments on 116 FSC-147 images demonstrate coherent element models capturing intra-category variability.

entry.title: Do Input-Level Defenses Transfer to Observation-Level Attacks on VideoLLMs?

author.name: Bangshuo Zhu, Wei Song, Yuxin Cao, Yuezhong Wu, Zhiquan Liu, Yuekang Li, Jingling Xue

entry.summary: This paper introduces DefTEval, a framework for evaluating whether existing input-level adversarial defenses can mitigate observation-level attacks on VideoLLMs, which exploit frame sampling, token compression, and modality fusion pipelines to hide harmful content from the model. The work addresses an unstudied gap in video model safety, since no defense currently targets this internal-representation attack surface. It matters for safe deployment of VideoLLMs in content moderation and video analytics.

entry.title: PIC: Revisiting INR for Image Coding with Fast Encoding and Sub-Millisecond Decoding

author.name: Xiang Liu, Jinxiang Wang, Bin Chen, Zimo Liu, Mingyao Hong, Jiawei Li, Yaowei Wang, Shu-tao Xia

entry.summary: PIC is a feedforward implicit neural representation (INR) image codec that computes all information needed by the INR network in a single forward pass, achieving 20 FPS encoding, paired with a highly optimized decoder reaching 2000 FPS. This overcomes the two main practical barriers of INR-based compression: slow per-image fitting during encoding and underutilized decoding efficiency. It matters because it makes neural image codecs competitive with or superior to JPEG in practical deployment.

entry.title: IM-ENGINE: Image Editing for Embodied Data Generation

author.name: Yian Wang, Junyi Cao, Xiaowen Qiu, Chuang Gan

entry.summary: IM-ENGINE uses image editing as an intermediate representation for embodied data generation: given a rendered scene with known geometry and camera parameters, it edits images to inject task-relevant semantics and recovers explicit 3D states using simulator priors. This bridges the gap between semantically rich but costly human demonstrations and scalable but behaviorally underspecified simulation. It promises cheaper, physically executable supervision for manipulation learning.

entry.title: Benchmarking Dexterity of Multifingered Robot Hands: A Review and Perspective

author.name: Anthony Shilati, Anunth Ramaswami, Luke Batteas, Sylvia Tan, Anthony Barcio, Sairam Umakanth, Preksha Rao, David McDougall, Landry Graves, Ahmet A. Ozkan, Yunsoo Yoon, Arushi Pradhan, Michael G. Henry, Rohan Kota, Damian Gonzalez, Gray C. Thomas, Gary K. Fedder, J. Edward Colgate, Kevin M. Lynch

entry.summary: A review from the NSF HAND Engineering Research Center surveying the state of the art in benchmarking multifingered robot hand dexterity, with emphasis on fine in-hand manipulation. It proposes a three-level benchmark framework intended to make dexterity evaluation rigorous and comparable across systems. Given that dexterity is a key bottleneck for physical AI, standardized benchmarks could shape research prioritization in robot manipulation.

entry.title: VLA-Corrector: Stage-Aware Observable State Understanding for Prompt-Based Closed-Loop Recovery of Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Chang Song, Bin Qian, Yan Feng, Zhijie Song

entry.summary: This paper introduces a stage-aware failure verification and prompt recovery framework that enables closed-loop correction of fixed Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies for long-horizon robot manipulation, without parameter updates or simulator access. A learned verifier estimates manipulation progress and execution risk from multi-view observations, proprioception, and action history to diagnose failures caused by action noise or object displacement. This addresses a key gap in deploying VLAs reliably outside lab settings.

entry.title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Songhua Yang (Wuhan University), Ziyu Liu (Wuhan University), Xuetao Li (Wuhan University), Ruqi Xiao (Wuhan University), Kangxin Zhu (Wuhan University), Miao Li (Institute of Technological Sciences, Wuhan University)

entry.summary: ICI-VLA equips a text-action VLM with few-shot test-time adaptation for new manipulation tasks via in-context demonstrations, avoiding gradient updates at deployment. It decomposes long trajectories into short semantically labeled micro-demonstrations and retrieves them at inference while keeping the policy fixed and retaining the native text-generation interface. This addresses rapid VLA deployment when task data and compute are scarce.

entry.title: Seeing is Not Believing: Breaking the Physical-to-Digital Trust Boundary in Robotics

author.name: Leming Shen, Shikai Geng, Yuanqing Zheng, Chris Xiaoxuan Lu

entry.summary: This security paper uncovers a severe ROS 2 vulnerability: by modifying a single environment variable, an adversary can covertly intercept and inject telemetry and control signals, hijacking a robot to perform dangerous tasks while spoofing downstream remote attestation with synthesized telemetry. It also exposes risks from widespread reliance on third-party components. The work demonstrates that remote attestation of physical robot behavior can be systematically deceived.

entry.title: Estimating Semantic Ambiguity via Gaussian Context Distributions for VLM-Driven Traversability Analysis

author.name: Ramona H\"auselmann, Mario A. V. Saucedo, Christoforos Kanellakis, George Nikolakopoulos

entry.summary: The authors propose a pipeline that grounds open-vocabulary vision-language model predictions onto a continuous physical traversability scale and models response uncertainty as a Gaussian Context Distribution. This yields dense traversability and uncertainty maps for unstructured-environment navigation. Validated on the real-world GOOSE dataset, it directly tackles VLM semantic ambiguity, a key failure mode for deploying foundation models on robots.

entry.title: A Lower Bound for the Heavy-Ball Method on Smooth Convex Functions

author.name: Jianhao Ma, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Proves that the classical Heavy-Ball method cannot achieve Nesterov's O(T^-2) last-iterate rate on smooth convex objectives even with fully horizon-dependent parameter schedules, establishing an Omega(1/(T^alpha log T)) lower bound with alpha the golden ratio. This settles a long-standing question about the fundamental limits of momentum tuning.

entry.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent

author.name: Yirong Zeng, Shen You, Jinhang Feng, Yufei Liu, Xiao Ding, Yutai Hou, Hao Cong, Yuxian Wang, Wu Ning, Wang Xu, Bibo Cai

entry.summary: EnvCraft is an automated framework for synthesizing executable, stateful environments and scalable training data for agentic reinforcement learning of long-horizon computer-use agents. It addresses the scarcity of interactive training environments beyond simple tool-calling endpoints.

entry.title: When Can LLM Digital Twins Reduce Human Measurement? From Behavioral Fidelity to Statistical Substitutability

author.name: Steven Wang, Kyle Hunt, Shaojie Tang, Kenneth Joseph

entry.summary: Proposes statistical substitutability as a rigorous criterion for when LLM-based digital twins of human respondents can actually replace human data collection while preserving valid statistical inference. The framework, grounded in mixed-subject and prediction-powered inference, evaluates substitutes along four dimensions including respondent-level signal and cross-population stability. This provides a principled answer to a question usually assessed only by aggregate correlation.

entry.title: Bridging the Semantic-Utility Gap in Multimodal RAG via Generator-in-the-Loop Alignment

author.name: Zhan-Lun Chang, Dong-Jun Han, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Mung Chiang, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage generator-in-the-loop alignment framework for multimodal RAG that closes the gap between semantic retrieval similarity and answer utility without human document-level annotations. Stage 1 uses a VLM to generate a hypothetical text passage from the image-query pair to bridge the modality gap, and Stage 2 aligns a cross-encoder reranker toward generator usefulness. This targets a well-recognized failure mode where relevant-looking documents do not improve answers.

entry.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Approximate Value Iteration in Self-Play

author.name: Raphael Boige, Amine Boumaza, Bruno Scherrer

entry.summary: This paper shows that a minimal self-play implementation of Approximate Value Iteration (AVI) learns more accurate value functions than AlphaZero-style methods in moderately sized games like Connect Four and 7x7 Hex, without MCTS overhead. One-step lookahead with the learned values proves competitive. This challenges assumptions about the necessity of heavy search in game-playing self-play systems.

entry.title: WolfSociety: Understanding Collective Risk from Harmful-Agent Scaling in Financial Agent Societies

author.name: Lejun Zhang, Sarah Lu-Liang, Xin Jiang, Muning Wen, Weinan Zhang, Shangding Gu

entry.summary: WolfSociety studies how collective failure emerges in multi-agent LLM societies as the fraction of harmful agents and the society size scale, using a controlled simulation where agents communicate over a social network and trade in a shared market. Results show failure is rare at low harmful fractions but rises sharply over a narrow threshold range, with the critical fraction shifting as society size grows from 100 to 2000 agents. This shifts safety evaluation from individual agents to collective dynamics.

entry.title: Steering Interference Reflects the Model's Defaults, Not the Behavior Directions

author.name: Srikanth Malla, Chiho Choi, Joon Hee Choi

entry.summary: Empirically shows that activation steering does not behave modularly: adding a behavior direction perturbs a small, model-specific set of default behaviors (refusal, sycophancy, poeticism) largely independent of which behavior is steered. Evidence spans 24 behaviors and ten instruction-tuned models, with effects measured by an LLM judge on generated text.

entry.title: AgentLeak: Cloning Stronger LLM Agent Capabilities onto Weaker Agents Beyond Skill Stealing

author.name: Xiaoting Lyu, Yuhong Wu, Yufei Han, Shichang Liu, Liang Zhang, Bin Wang, Bin Wang, Xiaobo Ma, Wei Wang

entry.summary: AgentLeak studies a new security threat: whether a weaker attacker-controlled agent can acquire a stronger proprietary agent's task-solving capability through limited black-box interaction, showing that leaking skill artifacts alone does not transfer capability without implicit procedural behaviors. The paper formalizes this capability-cloning attack surface beyond prior skill-stealing work. It raises timely IP and security concerns for deployed LLM agents.

entry.title: CodeTD: Topology of Attention Detects Hallucinations in Code LLMs

author.name: Daria Voronkova, Ilya Trofimov, Anton Dmitriev, Eduard Tulchinskii, Evgeny Burnaev, Serguei Barannikov

entry.summary: Introduces CodeTD, the first pre-execution code-hallucination detector based on topological data analysis of code LLM attention maps, quantifying prompt-generation mismatch. Evaluated on HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, and MultiPL-E across 5 languages and 10 code LLMs up to 34B parameters.

entry.title: 3DWay: Generalizing Robot Manipulation via 3D Consistent Waypoints

author.name: Ziqin Huang, Yingyue Li, Chenyangguang Zhang, Ruida Zhang, Yuxin Chen, Gu Wang, Xingyu Liu, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: 3DWay addresses 3D ambiguity in trajectory-based manipulation policies by predicting multi-view consistent 2D waypoints from images and then triangulating them into explicit 3D motion specifications. This bridges pretrained vision-language models and generalizable robot manipulation policies more reliably than 2D trajectory prediction. It is relevant to scaling robot learning with VLM backbones.

entry.title: Kairos: A Dataset for Fine-Grained Video-Language Modeling over Space, Time, and Dynamics

author.name: Ruibo Ming, Lei Sun, Deheng Zhang, He Zhang, Jialu Li, Jian Wang, Zhendong Li, Mengshun Hu, Danda Pani Paudel, Luc Van Gool, Jinjin Gu

entry.summary: Kairos is a new video-language dataset featuring long videos (10 to 30 minutes) annotated with fine-grained, time-resolved supervision covering ongoing actions, entity appearances and attributes, interactions, and evolving context. It aims to move video-language models beyond clip-level abstraction toward modeling continuous visual dynamics over extended time horizons. Datasets with dense temporal alignment are a key bottleneck for next-generation video understanding, so this resource could enable training and evaluation of temporally grounded video models.

entry.title: The Audit Decides the Verdict: Instrument Effects Rival Demographic Bias in LLM Decision Audits

author.name: Siddharth Vohra, Manikandan Ravikiran

entry.summary: Tests whether a previously reported rating-versus-ranking demographic bias reversal in LLM audits generalizes to hiring, lending, and medical triage using 40,726 requests across five models with a pre-registered design. None of 36 planned contrasts survives correction, suggesting the published reversal was largely an instrument effect. A valuable, rigorous replication-style study with implications for how LLM fairness audits should be designed.

entry.title: DataFlex-RL: An Evaluation Platform for RLVR Data Policies

author.name: Hao Liang, Mingrui Chen, Hengyi Feng, Meiyi Qiang, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: DataFlex-RL is a controlled evaluation platform comparing data-selection and reweighting policies for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards under a common GRPO recipe, using Qwen2.5-7B-Base across 12 math, logic, and science benchmarks. Strikingly, none of eight rollout-selection or reweighting methods beat uniform sampling with statistical significance. This negative result is valuable for the RLVR community, which has accumulated many heuristic data policies without rigorous comparison.

entry.title: LATS: Levy Adaptive Tree Sampling for Feedback-Driven Diverse Target Discovery

author.name: Binglin Ji, Anindya Sarkar, Hengchang Lu, Lecheng Kong, Yixin Chen, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik

entry.summary: Proposes LATS, a diffusion sampling method for scientific discovery that steers generation toward rare, high-utility tail regions revealed through sequential interactive feedback. It uses Levy-flight-inspired tree search to balance the pre-trained model's density bias against exploration under strict sampling budgets.

entry.title: Decomposition-Guided Diffusion Language Models for Inertial Confinement Fusion Prediction

author.name: Xiang Zhang, Varchas Gopalaswamy, Rahman Ejaz, Riccardo Betti, Dongfang Liu

entry.summary: ICF-DLM is claimed to be the first language-model-based predictor for inertial confinement fusion, inferring 512-step neutron-rate diagnostics directly from laser pulse and target parameters with fewer than 300 real training shots. It handles extreme temporal sparsity, scale mismatch, and picosecond peak sensitivity via physics-typed decomposition. High-value application given each National Ignition Facility shot costs roughly a million dollars.

entry.title: RoPE attention is an exact forward-pass gradient step with softmax intact

author.name: Julie Huang, Maggie Chlon, Leon Chlon

entry.summary: The authors derive an exact mathematical representation of the RoPE-softmax attention forward pass as a single gradient step on a query-conditioned quadratic objective, constructing a query-dependent effective matrix without approximating the softmax. They also connect the RoPE positional encoding generator to exact positional finite differences and derive tokenwise error bounds for reusing the representation.

entry.title: CONDUIT: A Unified Residual-Stream Restoration Framework for KV Cache Reuse in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Pengan Chen, Kaisheng Zheng, Liang Hong, Lixia Yi, Jiyue Jiang, Jiayang Chen, Yixuan Wang, Yimin Fan, Xinyuan Liu, Jiayi Li, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Yu Li

entry.summary: CONDUIT is a training-free policy for reusing key-value caches in vision-language models when the same visual content recurs under changed prefixes, framing selective token refresh as residual-stream restoration. It uses norm-weighted attention to rank stale tokens, avoiding failure modes of raw-attention selection such as wasting budget on high-attention but low-value tokens or query-irrelevant images. This targets a major inference cost in VLMs where expensive visual prefixes are repeatedly re-encoded.

entry.title: CEDAR: Error-Bounded Residual Routing for Efficient Long-Context Attention

author.name: Siyu Li, Dong Wang, Jie Zhou, Wei Li, Yang Xu, Sijie Song

entry.summary: Proposes CEDAR, a coarse-to-fine dynamic attention routing method for long-context prefill that keeps the language model frozen while preserving global coverage. Each semantic chunk contributes a cheap key-value summary to a residual attention path, and chunks with high estimated approximation error are expanded to exact token attention, with exact and summarized contributions combined in a single softmax. This recovers routing misses that hard sparse-attention selection cannot.

entry.title: Query-Oblivious Coresets for Softmax Attention: Improved Bounds and Efficient Constructions

author.name: Ofek I. Cohen

entry.summary: This theory paper closes a gap between upper and lower bounds on the size of query-oblivious coresets for softmax attention, resolving an open conjecture of Liberty, Andoni and Kleiner using a spherical lift that lets a chaining bound apply directly, plus Chevet's inequality. The result characterizes how small a key-value subset can be while approximating attention output for all queries within a ball. It is mathematically significant for the foundations of efficient attention approximation.

entry.title: CST-WM: A Causally Structured World Model for Embodied Visual Tracking

author.name: Junyi Hu, Shuaihang Yuan, Yi Fang

entry.summary: CST-WM builds a causally structured world model for embodied visual tracking that prevents causal hallucination, where action-conditioned predictors exploit spurious correlations between robot control and target observations instead of modeling action effects through robot motion. Framing tracking as predictive decision-making over future target observability is the key insight. This addresses a subtle but important failure mode in learned world models.

entry.title: Multi-Grid Post-Training for Long-Form Multi-Shot Video Generation

author.name: Jiawei Mao, Haoqin Tu, Hardy Chen, Yuhan Wang, Keyang Xu, Jieru Mei, Hongliang Fei, Ruogu Fang, Wei Shao, Cihang Xie, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes MovieGrid, a multi-grid post-training paradigm that decomposes long videos into temporally ordered chunks arranged on a spatial grid for joint modeling, improving within-shot motion coherence and cross-shot narrative consistency. It includes a 1,000-video Multi-Grid Long Video (MGLV) dataset construction pipeline.

entry.title: Mask Forcing: Improving Autoregressive Video Diffusion Distillation via Dual-Noise Masking Rollout

author.name: Zhuoran Zhao, Shengju Qian, Tongtong Liang, Xianghao Kong, Songchun Zhang, Junchao Huang, Guian Fang, Xin Wang, Pan Hui, Anyi Rao

entry.summary: Mask Forcing targets over-saturation and over-smoothing artifacts in autoregressive video diffusion models distilled from bidirectional teachers via Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD). The authors diagnose the cause as mode-seeking reverse-KL collapse and propose a Dual-Noise Masking Rollout strategy that perturbs the AR student self-rollout to mitigate mode collapse. It matters because real-time video generation quality is a key bottleneck for diffusion-based streaming video systems.

entry.title: Observation Design for Certified Control Authority: Projection--Estimability Separation and Active-Face Equivalence

author.name: Guangxi Wan, Hualong Du, Yuqi Liu, Qingwei Dong, Qingxin Li, Hongfei Bai, Peng Zeng

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies how sensor observations should be designed to maximize the set of actions a runtime safety admission gate can certify. It proves a projection-estimability separation showing that constraint directions with components in the information matrix range become arbitrarily verifiable while nullspace components make robust action admission impossible at any budget, and characterizes when mixed directions are generic. This gives safety-critical systems a principled link between observability design and certifiable control authority.

entry.title: Building safe physical AI: Open questions, risks, and a call for collaboration

author.name: benjaminalt

entry.summary: A research agenda laying out open safety questions for physical AI (robots, drones), arguing that inherently multimodal, physically-embodied frontier systems require new alignment techniques, interpretability tools, and evals, plus scalable generation of simulated and real-world safety data. It calls for collaboration between the AI safety community and robotics developers.

entry.title: ARC-Bench: Closed-Loop Replanning Masks Broken Action Ranking in Frozen JEPA World Models

author.name: Zhengshu Zhang, Zhiyuan Li

entry.summary: ARC-Bench is a no-leak, fixed-candidate protocol auditing whether frozen JEPA-style world models rank candidate actions correctly by latent-distance-to-goal, applied to official released JEPA-WM checkpoints across navigation and manipulation tasks. The core finding is that the latent-closeness action-ranking assumption fails severely and structurally in manipulation settings, with closed-loop replanning masking the broken rankings.

entry.title: More Than Mimicking Reviewers: Evaluating LLMs for Pre-Submission Peer Review

author.name: Pouya Parsa, Amin Rezaei

entry.summary: This paper evaluates an author-facing LLM system that generates a broad pool of atomic review concerns and compresses them into a short pre-submission report, tested on 3,398 ICLR 2026 manuscripts. On a diagnostic set, independent sampling covered 44.9% of historical reviewer issues, rising to 78.7% strict and 84.9% seriousness-weighted coverage after deduplication and refill, at notable compute cost.

entry.title: Generator-Independent Runtime Assurance under Partial Observation

author.name: Guangxi Wan, Yongbo Xie, Yuqi Liu, Qingwei Dong, Qingxin Li, Hongfei Bai, Peng Zeng

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies when closed-loop safety guarantees for proposal-based controllers (learned policies, LLM planners) behind runtime verification gates decouple from the generator. It proves that per-candidate certification inflates false-admission risk under retry or best-of-k selection, and that setwise soundness is necessary and sufficient for generator-independent admission soundness.

entry.title: SCIRIGOR:Evaluating Open-Ended Scientific Analysis Beyond Final Scores

author.name: Bowen Liu, Shuo Nie, Bodong Du, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: Introduces SciRIGOR, a benchmark of 100 cases across six scientific domains evaluating whether coding agents produce evidence-grounded analyses where claims are supported by results and figures from the same run. The framework builds typed evidence graphs, separates artifact fidelity from relational validity, and localizes the earliest unsupported claim. Addresses a real gap in evaluating agent reasoning quality beyond final-answer scoring.

entry.title: NormViz: A Benchmark and Framework for Grounding Multimodal Reasoning in Global Cultures

author.name: Akhila Yerukola, Fabrice Y Harel-Canada, Simran Khanuja, Abhinav Sukumar Rao, Ashima Suvarna, Nanyun Peng, Saadia Gabriel, Maarten Sap

entry.summary: Introduces NormViz-Bench, a human-validated benchmark of 3,268 contrastive image pairs across 16 countries testing visual norm understanding: whether models can reason about how culturally specific behaviors change image interpretation (conforming, violating, or irrelevant). Extends cultural AI evaluation beyond text and artifact recognition to situated social-norm reasoning. Backed by a strong academic team.

entry.title: Beyond Sparse Rewards: A New Benchmark and Structure-Aware Graph Alignment for Micro-Drama Understanding

author.name: Yixin Qin, Shi-Zhe Chen, Zhiqi Yu, Siyuan Cheng, Tao Cheng, Jinwen Luo, Zheng Wei

entry.summary: Introduces M-Drama, the first large-scale bilingual benchmark for micro-drama video understanding with over 35K instances across 9,138 ultra-short, densely plotted clips, and proposes SAGA, a structure-aware graph alignment reward that models narratives as heterogeneous graphs to produce dense RL rewards capturing character identities and temporal structure. Together they enable reinforcement-learning improvements for VLMs on complex short-form narratives.

entry.title: The Emerging AI Paper-Review Arms Race: Adversarial Co-Evolution in Scholarly Publishing

author.name: Chenguang Wang, Ming Li, Adebayo Braimah, Chenrui Fan, Tuo Wang, Weijie Guan, Ruiyi Zhang, Tianyi Zhou, Dawei Zhou

entry.summary: A synthesis of 230 publications organizing the AI-driven transformation of scholarly publishing into six connected dynamics: production scaling, evaluation automation, evaluation manipulation, defense mechanisms, evasion, and long-horizon ecosystem feedback. It argues AI-produced research and AI-based review must be studied as a co-evolving adversarial system.

entry.title: Quantization Amplifies Determinism, Not Bias: Scale-Dependent Behavioral Effects of Serving-Time Weight Compression

author.name: Dachi Kurtskhalia

entry.summary: Serving three Qwen3 checkpoints (8B/14B/32B) at three precisions with hardware, software, and sampling held constant, the study collects about 71,000 seed-paired completions to test whether quantization changes which valid answer a model chooses. Findings indicate 4-bit quantization reduces output diversity at smaller scale rather than introducing bias, challenging the notion that int4 is behaviorally free.

entry.title: Eliciting Self-Verification in Multimodal Reasoning Agents with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Vishwas Sathish, Viresh Ranjan, Xinliang Zhu, Arnab Dhua, Douglas Gray

entry.summary: The paper presents SVRL, an RL-only finetuning framework that trains multimodal agents to verify and filter noisy retrieved evidence (e.g., from web search) within their own reasoning traces, without external verifier modules. Building on GRPO-style methods, it extends reliable tool-use RL from text-only math and coding domains to multimodal agents operating under sparse outcome-level supervision. This matters because trustworthy tool integration in multimodal settings is a key bottleneck for real-world agent deployment.

entry.title: OntologyBench: Can Dense Retrieval Satisfy Structured Biomedical Constraints?

author.name: Xiao Yu Cindy Zhang, Wyeth Wasserman, Jian Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces OntologyBench, a large tiered biomedical retrieval benchmark with over 597,000 relevance pairs covering concept grounding, relational retrieval, and compositional phenotype-based retrieval against structured ontology constraints. Findings show embeddings degrade on relational and compositional tasks, ontology-derived fine-tuning helps, and reranking or LLM-based candidate scoring adds little end-to-end value. It exposes a concrete weakness of dense retrieval on structured constraint satisfaction.

entry.title: Good Pretraining, Bad SFT: Checkpoint Quality Across the Training Stack

author.name: Sohir Maskey, Philipp Scholl, Jonas Knupp, Pit Neitemeier, Sascha Wirges

entry.summary: This paper shows that selecting language-model checkpoints by pretraining loss or benchmark scores can fail at scale: in a full 30B mixture-of-experts training pipeline, the best checkpoint after downstream training is not the one with the best pretraining metrics. Instead, better downstream checkpoints exhibit higher solution density, meaning they retain performance under local weight perturbations. This matters because it challenges standard checkpoint-selection practice and offers solution density as a better selection signal.

entry.title: When Do Options Help? Policy Necrosis and Redundant Coverage in Option-Critic

author.name: Bingyun Liu, Yuheng Jing

entry.summary: This paper provides theory and experiments explaining when and why options (temporal abstractions) help in the option-critic reinforcement learning framework, showing that the learned termination rule contributes nothing and can even block exploration with Omega(T) regret in some instances. It introduces the notions of policy necrosis and redundant coverage, and shows that forcing termination at every step can preserve the headline benefit of adding more options. This is a valuable critical analysis of a widely used hierarchical RL method.

entry.title: UniRRM: Unified Reasoning Reward Models Across Languages and Evaluation Paradigms

author.name: Peng Lai, Yichao Du, Junchao Wu, Weibo Gao, Linan Yue, Longyue Wang, Weihua Luo, Derek F. Wong, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: This work introduces MixReward, a large-scale multilingual reward dataset spanning six domains and 103 languages with pairwise and listwise data, and UniRRM, a unified reasoning reward model supporting multiple evaluation paradigms. It targets the reliability gap in open-ended-task rewards, avoiding reliance on costly proprietary LLM-as-a-Judge systems or opaque scalar reward models.

entry.title: DART: Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training for Algorithm Learning

author.name: Hieu Tran Bao, Phung Thanh Dang, Pham Quang Nhat Minh, Hoang Thanh Tung

entry.summary: Proposes DART, a training framework for recurrent reasoning models that replaces single-point ground-truth supervision with a local target distribution aligned via an adversarial objective. This provides richer learning signal for hard structured problems where valid solutions are sparse, yielding more stable iterative trajectories.

entry.title: Tri-PvP: Exposing Modality Bias in Omni-Modal Large Language Models through Perceptual-Propositional Evidence Conflicts

author.name: Yen-Ting Piao, Shu-Yun Chen, Chin-Hui Chu, Chun-Wei Chen, Shih-Yun Shan Kuan, Hung-yi Lee, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: Tri-PvP is an 8,000-sample tri-modal conflict benchmark that separates perceptual evidence (photos, recordings) from propositional evidence (declarative claims) across vision, audio, and text to cleanly attribute modality bias in omni-modal LLMs. Evaluations of five OLLMs reveal robust visual bias across models.

entry.title: SCRIPTIOC-BENCH: A Benchmark for Recognizing Actionable Threat Intelligence from Script-Based Malware using LLMs

author.name: Hanna Kim, Jian Cui, Minkyoo Song, Hwanjo Heo, Seungwon Shin, Kimin Lee, Xiaojing Liao

entry.summary: Presents SCRIPTIOC-BENCH, 634 manually verified JavaScript, PowerShell, and VBScript malware samples for measuring LLM ability to statically recover indicators of compromise (URLs, domains, IPs, filesystem artifacts) that may be dispersed or transformed within malicious code.

entry.title: Detokenization Leaks: Reconstructing Local LLM Outputs From Cache Traces

author.name: Roy Weiss, Benyamin Konstantinov, Eitam Sheetrit, Tomer Simon, Yisroel Mirsky

entry.summary: Presents a side-channel attack that reconstructs text generated by locally hosted LLMs from CPU cache activity during detokenization, using Flush+Reload and Prime+Probe to isolate token-dependent signals plus a clustering-and-language-model pipeline for recovery. The attack works under default inference pipelines across datasets and hardware platforms, requiring no deployment-specific assumptions.

entry.title: Noisy-Space Policy Gradient for Diffusion Policies in Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mahmoud Selim, Cristina Cipriani, Karl H. Johansson

entry.summary: This paper tackles the difficult integration of diffusion policies with reinforcement learning by defining a noisy-space action-value function over diffusion latents. From this construction it derives a noisy-space policy gradient (NSPG) that optimizes latents using clean action-space value estimates, plus a KL-regularized policy improvement objective admitting a diffusion-compatible form. This offers a principled theoretical foundation for RL with diffusion policies in offline settings.

entry.title: Discovering Natural Transformation Vulnerabilities in Black-Box Vision Models

author.name: Dongsu Song, DaeYun GO, Jay Hoon Jung

entry.summary: The Adversarial Scenario Attack (ASA) is a query-based black-box framework that uses a multimodal language model and text-guided image editing to search natural-language transformation scenarios (background, weather, material) exposing vision model failures, avoiding surrogate models or costly optimization. It extends adversarial robustness analysis to realistic semantic changes discovered automatically. This reveals vulnerabilities that norm-bounded perturbation studies miss.

entry.title: Flow3D-OPD: Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for 3D Geometry Generation with Flow-Matching Diffusion Transformer

author.name: Zhiwei Ning, Zhen Zhou, Puhua Jiang, Xintong Han, Gengming Zhang, Jie Yang, Zhonglong Zheng, Yuanjie Zheng, Wei Liu, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: Flow3D-OPD is a two-stage post-training framework applying multi-teacher on-policy distillation to image-to-3D flow-matching DiT models, sidestepping reward-design and gradient-interference problems that plague RL-based post-training for 3D quality. It transfers a technique proven in LLMs and image generation to 3D geometry generation. This addresses a genuinely underexplored post-training bottleneck for high-fidelity 3D asset creation.

entry.title: Latent-to-Latent Flow for Volumetric Stochastic Segmentation

author.name: Omar Todd, Sooha Kim, Raghav Mehta, Katherine Mackay, David Bernstein, Alexandra Taylor, Fabio De Sousa Ribeiro, Ben Glocker

entry.summary: The paper introduces a latent-to-latent flow matching technique for stochastic segmentation of 3D medical volumes, capturing inter-observer variability by operating in latent representations of both image and label space.
